finding_title: NAA20 perturbation couples recurrent CYP46A1 repression to induction of sterol-synthesis transcripts
core_idea: In the atlas, Naa20 CRISPR perturbation lowered Cyp46a1 in thalamic, midbrain glutamatergic, and midbrain/pons/medulla GABAergic neurons, while sterol-synthesis transcripts rose in hypothalamic and midbrain/pons/medulla contexts. The biological interpretation is that impaired NatB function may reduce neuronal cholesterol elimination through CYP46A1 and elicit compensatory sterol synthesis; the co-occurrence of Cyp46a1 repression and Fdft1 induction in 191 MB P MY GABA makes this a testable coupling rather than an inference from cross-context absence.
significance: If confirmed at the protein and metabolite levels, this would connect NAA20-associated neurodevelopmental disease to the principal route of brain cholesterol disposal, reframing NatB pathology around a NAA20–CYP46A1–24S-hydroxycholesterol axis. That would justify an unusually broad research direction spanning NatB substrate acetylation, neuronal sterol flux, circuit consequences, disease biomarkers, and therapeutic restoration of cholesterol turnover.
prior_expectation: Before viewing the atlas, impaired NAA20/NatB activity was expected to cause recessive neurodevelopmental disease based on human genetics and biochemical evidence (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34230638/), while CYP46A1 was independently understood as the major route for converting brain cholesterol to 24S-hydroxycholesterol in a review of brain cholesterol turnover (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/27663182/). Those established facts did not predict that acute neuronal Naa20 perturbation would repeatedly repress Cyp46a1 or pair that response with sterol-synthesis induction.
support_and_caveats: Naa20 perturbation reduced Cyp46a1 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut (log2FC -0.39135, FDR 1.29e-13), 155 MB Glut (-0.76576, FDR 1.03e-10), and 191 MB P MY GABA (-1.03665, FDR 2.55e-6). Sterol-pathway increases included Cyp51 in 145 MH-LH TH Glut (+0.56858, FDR 0.0272), Mvk in the same class (+1.05342, FDR 0.0339), and Fdft1 in 191 MB P MY GABA (+1.02478, FDR 1.79e-5), where Cyp46a1 was also reduced. The major alternative is an indirect stress response to NAA20 perturbation rather than a sterol-regulatory role of NatB; the experiment measured neither N-terminal acetylation, CYP46A1 protein, 24S-hydroxycholesterol, nor cholesterol flux, and the partial sterol response was not identical across neuronal classes.
research_community: NatB/N-terminal-acetylation researchers, brain-cholesterol biologists, and investigators of NAA20-related neurodevelopmental disease would have the clearest reason to revise their working models. The pivotal test is neuron-resolved Naa20 editing coupled to CYP46A1 protein and isotope-based cholesterol-to-24S-hydroxycholesterol flux, with CRISPR-resistant wild-type and catalytically inactive NAA20 resolving NatB dependence from generic editing stress. A verified causal chain would establish an unusually broad agenda spanning the neuronal N-terminal acetylome, lipid turnover, circuit dysfunction, patient metabolite biomarkers, and CYP46A1-directed rescue.

finding_title: MATR3 perturbation induces an RBP state that active FUS and TDP-43 perturbations do not reproduce
core_idea: Across cortical, thalamic, midbrain glutamatergic, and posterior GABAergic neurons, Matr3 perturbation repeatedly increased Atp9b, Ddhd1, E2f4, Kcnq2, Sugp2, Uggt2, and Zkscan3 while decreasing Rsrp1. FUS and TDP-43 perturbations generated substantial expression responses in matched classes but did not reproduce this signed MATR3 module. This observed divergence supports the interpretation that acute MATR3 reduction exposes an RNA-binding-protein liability state rather than a generic response to perturbing any ALS-linked RBP.
significance: This relationship argues that MATR3-associated disease should not be subsumed under a single TDP-43/FUS stress model. If the module reflects direct MATR3-dependent RNA regulation, it would create a distinct mechanistic and biomarker framework for MATR3-linked ALS, frontotemporal degeneration, and distal myopathy, and would motivate comparative studies of why disease-associated RBPs converge in some settings yet diverge sharply in mature neurons.
prior_expectation: MATR3 was already known as a nuclear RNA-binding protein associated with neuromuscular disease and selective neuronal vulnerability (https://doi.org/10.1172/jci.insight.143948), with additional evidence connecting its perturbation to neurodegenerative RNA dysregulation (https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-020-18949-w). Recent work also provided precedent for convergence among ALS-associated RNA-binding proteins on a REST–UNC13A mechanism (https://doi.org/10.1038/s44318-025-00506-0), so a shared acute response would have been reasonable before the atlas; the recurrent, oppositely signed MATR3 module was not.
support_and_caveats: In 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, Matr3 perturbation increased Atp9b (+1.06061, FDR 4.14e-12), Ddhd1 (+1.59396, FDR 4.23e-14), and E2f4 (+1.29225, FDR 4.72e-8) and decreased Rsrp1 (-0.35285, FDR 1.96e-4). The same directions were stronger in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut: Atp9b +1.48175 (FDR 3.53e-38), Ddhd1 +1.76597 (FDR 2.64e-49), E2f4 +1.73480 (FDR 1.46e-35), and Rsrp1 -0.69262 (FDR 1.26e-29). In 155 MB Glut, Ddhd1 rose +1.93699 (FDR 2.84e-28) and Rsrp1 fell -0.51681 (FDR 1.09e-14); in 191 MB P MY GABA, Ddhd1 (+1.89191, FDR 1.43e-11), E2f4 (+2.23139, FDR 1.42e-11), and Atp9b (+0.94914, FDR 0.00455) remained significant, although Rsrp1 did not (FDR 0.377). By comparison, Fus was strongly reduced in 151 (-1.40691, FDR 1.04e-45) yet Atp9b and Ddhd1 had FDR 1.0 and Rsrp1 moved oppositely upward (+0.42834, FDR 4.84e-29); Tardbp was likewise reduced (-1.41422, FDR 1.60e-39) while Rsrp1 increased (+0.15504, FDR 3.24e-5). The chief limitation is that guide efficiency and acute perturbation biology can generate apparent divergence; gene-level snRNA-seq does not measure the splicing, RNA export, binding occupancy, or aggregation mechanisms expected of these proteins.
research_community: ALS/FTD and neuromuscular-disease researchers—especially those studying MATR3 and comparative RBP biology—would be most likely to change direction. Matched-efficiency MATR3, FUS, and TARDBP editing in the same neuron types, followed by long-read RNA sequencing, MATR3 eCLIP, and CRISPR-resistant MATR3 rescue, would determine whether the signed module is a direct MATR3 regulon or a product of unequal perturbation or generic stress. Direct target recovery would justify MATR3-specific vulnerability maps, molecular biomarkers, and RNA-targeted interventions instead of a universal ALS-RBP model.

finding_title: PPP2R1A perturbation reverses sterol-transcription polarity across neuronal classes
core_idea: Ppp2r1a perturbation induced multiple cholesterol-biosynthesis genes in midbrain and hypothalamic glutamatergic neurons but reduced Srebf2 and Hmgcr in thalamic and cortical glutamatergic neurons. The observation therefore supports a testable interpretation in which the PP2A A-alpha scaffold gates qualitatively different sterol-homeostatic states across mature neuronal classes rather than producing one uniform cholesterol response.
significance: A validated polarity switch would make PP2A holoenzyme context an important determinant of neuronal lipid regulation, connecting phosphatase composition to opposing SREBP-pathway outputs. This could launch mechanistic studies of which PP2A complexes, phosphorylation events, and neuronal states determine sterol synthesis, and could alter how PPP2R1A-associated neurodevelopmental phenotypes or PP2A-directed interventions are interpreted.
prior_expectation: A curated cholesterol-biosynthesis pathway (https://reactome.org/content/detail/R-HSA-191273) places SREBP2/HMGCR control and downstream enzymes such as MSMO1, DHCR24, and SC5D within a coordinated sterol program. Before the atlas, a perturbation affecting that pathway would more naturally have been expected to shift the module in a common direction; prior knowledge did not predict opposite PPP2R1A-associated RNA outputs among these neuronal classes.
support_and_caveats: After Ppp2r1a perturbation, 155 MB Glut neurons increased Msmo1 (+1.01390, FDR 2.95e-9), Insig1 (+0.93877, FDR 4.72e-7), Dhcr24 (+0.81862, FDR 7.79e-7), and Sc5d (+0.75365, FDR 1.10e-6). The 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut class showed the same direction for Insig1 (+0.93884, FDR 1.69e-5), Sc5d (+0.81201, FDR 1.42e-4), Dhcr24 (+0.76304, FDR 2.67e-4), and Msmo1 (+0.82738, FDR 6.80e-4). Conversely, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut reduced Srebf2 (-0.53092, FDR 9.47e-8) and Hmgcr (-0.32009, FDR 0.0291), while 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut reduced Hmgcr (-0.59273, FDR 3.17e-5) and Srebf2 (-0.27908, FDR 0.0414). Because different genes mark the two arms, this is a pathway-level polarity interpretation rather than a literal sign reversal of every transcript; PP2A holoenzyme composition, phosphoproteins, SREBP2 cleavage, and sterol abundance were not measured, and unequal editing or baseline state remains an alternative.
research_community: PP2A signaling researchers, neuronal lipid biologists, and investigators of PPP2R1A-related developmental disorders are the natural audience. Their critical experiment is matched Ppp2r1a editing in purified representatives of the opposing neuronal classes, with phosphoproteomics, nuclear SREBP2 quantification, isotope-resolved sterol synthesis, and wild-type rescue. Opposite biochemical flux at comparable engagement would establish a phosphatase-dependent switch and motivate systematic mapping of PP2A holoenzymes to lipid-control nodes and neuronal physiology.

finding_title: AP2M1 and AP2S1 perturbations converge on TFRC induction and sterol repression while AP2S1 adds cortical activity-gene loss
core_idea: Perturbing either of two physical AP-2 subunits induced Tfrc and reduced sterol-regulatory transcripts in matched thalamic and midbrain neuronal classes; Ap2s1 perturbation additionally repressed an Arc/Egr3/Bdnf/Vgf branch in cortical neurons. Together, these observations suggest that neuronal AP-2 dysfunction may couple impaired cargo endocytosis to an iron-uptake compensation signal and lipid regulation, with a further AP2S1-associated activity-output branch.
significance: The convergence links a core endocytic complex to coordinated neuronal iron-receptor, sterol, and excitability-associated RNA outputs rather than treating AP-2 disease solely as defective vesicle trafficking. If validated, it would create a tractable iron–lipid–activity framework for AP2M1 developmental and epileptic encephalopathy and related AP-2 disorders, with distinct opportunities for cargo-level and neuronal-class interventions.
prior_expectation: AP2M1 and AP2S1 were already established as physical subunits of the AP-2 clathrin adaptor (https://rest.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P84091), and AP-2 depletion was known to impair transferrin-receptor uptake (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/12952941/). AP2M1 dysfunction is also linked to developmental and epileptic encephalopathy (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/31104773/). Those findings made defective endocytosis expected, but did not predict shared neuronal Tfrc induction with sterol repression or the AP2S1-associated cortical activity-gene branch.
support_and_caveats: In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Ap2m1 perturbation induced Tfrc (+0.83140, FDR 3.13e-6), and Ap2s1 perturbation induced it even more strongly (+0.98358, FDR 3.06e-24); both target transcripts were reduced in this class (Ap2m1 -0.57819, FDR 2.41e-8; Ap2s1 -0.53643, FDR 6.33e-5). In 155 MB Glut, Ap2m1 perturbation increased Tfrc (+0.96399, FDR 1.07e-5) while reducing Srebf2 (-0.78418, FDR 3.60e-5) and Dhcr24 (-0.83428, FDR 0.00323); Ap2s1 perturbation showed the same pattern for Tfrc (+0.85038, FDR 1.00e-7), Srebf2 (-0.49178, FDR 0.00229), and Dhcr24 (-0.55046, FDR 0.0146). The additional 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut Ap2s1 response included Egr3 -1.33292 (FDR 1.35e-13), Arc -0.89254 (FDR 2.56e-7), Bdnf -1.10465 (FDR 0.0274), and Vgf -0.63317 (FDR 2.52e-4). Convergence of two subunits argues against a single-guide artifact, but the assay did not measure coated pits, surface TFRC, iron uptake, cholesterol, or firing; generic membrane stress and unequal perturbation strength remain alternatives.
research_community: Endocytosis and membrane-trafficking researchers, neuronal iron and cholesterol biologists, and AP2M1 encephalopathy investigators have the strongest stake in this relationship. Comparing AP2M1- and AP2S1-edited neurons by live transferrin internalization, surface-TFRC imaging, labile-iron measurements, SREBP2 processing, lipidomics, and subunit-specific rescue would distinguish compensation for AP-2 cargo failure from a generic transcriptional stress state. The resulting cargo-to-state map could organize work on neuronal lipid balance, excitability, and genotype-specific therapeutic vulnerabilities.

finding_title: PGK1 and GAPDH perturbations converge on OGT and nuclear-speckle transcript loss
core_idea: Independent Pgk1 and Gapdh perturbations reduced Ogt together with Pnisr/Rsrp1-associated RNA-processing transcripts in thalamic glutamatergic neurons, and Tpi1 perturbation also reduced Ogt in hypothalamic glutamatergic neurons. These observations motivate, but do not establish, a mechanism linking adjacent lower-glycolysis steps to O-GlcNAc regulation and nuclear-speckle or RNA-processing maintenance; the response is not demonstrated for every glycolytic enzyme.
significance: This convergence offers a specific route by which glycolytic insufficiency could remodel neuronal RNA processing rather than merely lowering cellular energy. If flux, O-GlcNAc signaling, and splice regulation prove causally linked, the finding would support a substantial metabolism-to-RNA-biology program relevant to neuronal stress and metabolic neurological disease.
prior_expectation: GAPDH and PGK1 were known as adjacent enzymes in cytosolic glycolysis (https://reactome.org/content/detail/R-HSA-70171), and TPI1 as the enzyme interconverting DHAP and G3P in the glycolytic pathway (https://reactome.org/content/detail/R-HSA-70454). PNISR, RSRP1, SRRM2, and related readouts had curated nuclear-speckle or spliceosome annotations (https://www.uniprot.org/). Before the atlas, these facts did not predict that distinct lower-glycolysis perturbations would converge on Ogt and a compact RNA-processing transcript set in neurons.
support_and_caveats: In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Pgk1 perturbation reduced its own transcript (-1.44092, FDR 4.43e-32), Pnisr (-0.22694, FDR 7.00e-11), and Ogt (-0.14565, FDR 4.998e-4). Gapdh perturbation in the same class independently reduced Pnisr (-0.25522, FDR 2.19e-5), Rsrp1 (-0.19735, FDR 1.49e-4), and Ogt (-0.17676, FDR 0.0220). Tpi1 perturbation reduced Ogt in 145 MH-LH TH Glut (-0.38744, FDR 0.0121), although its secondary 151 RNA-processing changes were only nominal. GAPDH itself was absent from the measured features, metabolic flux and UDP-GlcNAc/O-GlcNAc levels were not assayed, and the modest effect sizes leave shared energy stress or altered cell state as important alternatives to a specific glycolysis–OGT mechanism.
research_community: Neuro-metabolism, O-GlcNAc, and RNA-splicing communities—particularly investigators of metabolic control over nuclear organization—would pursue this connection. Isotope tracing, ATP and UDP-GlcNAc measurements, quantitative O-GlcNAc proteomics, live speckle imaging, and long-read RNA sequencing after matched PGK1 and GAPDH perturbations would locate the defect; restoration by a defined metabolite or OGT rescue would separate causal signaling from nonspecific stress. The larger opportunity is a map of metabolic nodes that govern neuronal RNA processing and create disease-selective liabilities.

finding_title: STXBP1 perturbation produces distinct cortical, midbrain, and Pvalb transcriptional outputs
core_idea: Stxbp1 perturbation elicited a cortical Nrsn1/Pcsk1n-high and Grin2b-low response, a midbrain Cntnap1-low and Mt1/Fos-high response, and Slc6a1 repression in Pvalb GABA neurons. The biological interpretation is that chronic Munc18-1 insufficiency may be translated into different adaptive or stress states across neuronal classes rather than one transcriptomic consequence of presynaptic failure.
significance: STXBP1 disorders are often framed around a common vesicle-release defect; these distinct positive RNA outputs nominate neuronal-class-specific routes from that shared lesion to circuit pathology. Validation could redirect disease studies toward differential cortical, midbrain, and inhibitory-neuron compensation and create class-specific biomarkers or therapeutic endpoints for STXBP1 encephalopathy.
prior_expectation: STXBP1/Munc18-1 was established as a syntaxin-binding Sec1/Munc18 protein (https://rest.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P61764) required for neurotransmitter release (https://doi.org/10.1126/science.287.5454.864), and SNARE-complex biology (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/19164740/) predicted severe presynaptic dysfunction after its loss. That prior biology predicted a shared release defect, but not the distinct cortical neurosecretory, midbrain stress/adhesion, and Pvalb transporter RNA outputs observed here.
support_and_caveats: In 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, Stxbp1 perturbation reduced Stxbp1 (-0.520, FDR 9.66e-11) and Grin2b (-0.231, FDR 0.00582) while increasing Nrsn1 (+0.724, FDR 3.98e-4) and Pcsk1n (+0.448, FDR 5.87e-4). In 155 MB Glut, Stxbp1 was reduced (-0.608, FDR 2.76e-9), Cntnap1 decreased (-0.526, FDR 3.71e-5), and Mt1 (+1.107, FDR 9.47e-4) and Fos (+1.390, FDR 0.0464) increased. In 052 Pvalb Gaba, Stxbp1 perturbation lowered Slc6a1 (-0.412, FDR 1.27e-8); direct Slc6a1 perturbation strongly reduced its own transcript (-1.018, FDR 1.39e-29) without establishing that the broader STXBP1 mechanism runs through SLC6A1. The atlas measured steady-state nuclear RNA rather than release, firing, survival, or network activity, so different activity histories, effective power, and perturbation strength could explain part of the apparent class divergence.
research_community: STXBP1 encephalopathy researchers, synaptic-release biologists, and circuit physiologists have the clearest incentive to follow this finding. In genetically identified cortical, midbrain, and Pvalb neurons, optical release measurements, patch clamp, time-resolved single-cell RNA, and STXBP1 restoration should determine whether the RNA branches persist at matched degrees of release failure. A true class-dependent adaptation would provide a framework linking distinct molecular responses to seizure, movement, and cognitive phenotypes and to tailored rescue strategies.

finding_title: Acute TBR1 perturbation recurrently raises CPNE6 while splitting mature cortical projection-neuron outputs
core_idea: Acute Tbr1 perturbation increased Cpne6 in several cortical projection-neuron classes, coupled to Dkk3/Epb41 decreases in L5/6 intratelencephalic neurons but to Cacna1g/C1qtnf4 increases in NP-CT-L6b-OB neurons. A plausible interpretation is that TBR1 retains a mature synaptic and membrane-associated regulon whose output depends on projection-neuron identity and is separable from its canonical neonatal fate-specification role.
significance: A direct adult TBR1 regulon would extend TBR1 biology beyond developmental layer specification and provide a route from a neurodevelopmental transcription factor to ongoing projection-neuron physiology. This could launch focused studies of adult TBR1 chromatin occupancy, synaptic maintenance, and whether disease alleles perturb mature functions independently of early cortical wiring.
prior_expectation: Established work positioned TBR1 as a regulator of cortical projection-neuron and layer-6 identity (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/11239428/), showed continuing dosage-sensitive roles in postnatal cortical neurons (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30318412/), and linked TBR1 mutations to autism (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25232744/). Before viewing the atlas, one might therefore have expected acute postnatal perturbation either to reuse familiar developmental targets or to have little mature-neuron output; a recurrent Cpne6-centered, class-split response was not the standard prediction.
support_and_caveats: In 001 L5-6 IT Glut, Tbr1 perturbation decreased Dkk3 (-1.17698, FDR 0.00229) and Epb41 (-1.54013, FDR 0.00724) while increasing Cpne6 (+0.91271, FDR 0.00748). In 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, Cpne6 again increased (+0.60600, FDR 0.0237) and Dkk3 decreased (-0.71992, FDR 0.0360). By contrast, the 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut response was all upward among the reported rows, including Cacna1g +1.43196 (FDR 1.12e-5), Cpne6 +1.24500 (FDR 5.98e-5), and C1qtnf4 +0.47990 (FDR 0.0249). These are small expression programs from unequally sampled classes, and the assay did not measure TBR1 occupancy or direct transcription; residual lineage state, editing differences, or an indirect activity response could explain the split, while absence of neonatal targets is only a developmental comparison rather than a matched negative perturbation.
research_community: Cortical-development, projection-neuron, TBR1-syndrome, and activity-dependent-transcription communities would be most interested. Adult-neuron TBR1 CUT&RUN or CUT&Tag paired with nascent RNA after acute editing in the two responsive projection classes—and then CRISPR-resistant rescue—can distinguish direct occupancy at Cpne6, Dkk3/Epb41, or Cacna1g/C1qtnf4 from secondary state change. That result would let the field separate developmental from maintenance functions of TBR1 and test how patient variants alter adult cortical circuits.

finding_title: Zbtb11 perturbation recurrently lowers Rbm28, Stx16, Acsf3, and Ndufaf1 across subcortical neurons
core_idea: A recurrent downregulated core followed Zbtb11 perturbation in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA neurons, spanning Acsf3 and Ndufaf1, the nucleolar factor Rbm28, the trafficking factor Stx16, and the GPI-biosynthesis gene Pigq. This observation raises the biological interpretation that functional ZBTB11 disruption couples nuclear control of mitochondrial capacity to nucleolar, glycan, and endomembrane maintenance rather than affecting mitochondrial transcripts alone.
significance: If this coupling is real, it would give ZBTB11-associated intellectual disability a tractable multi-compartment neuronal mechanism and justify a substantial program linking mitochondrial output, ribosome biogenesis, membrane trafficking, and glycan biology. The atlas adds a recurrent neuronal RNA state and specific readouts for testing how ACSF3-related biochemistry fits into the broader syndrome.
prior_expectation: ZBTB11 was already expected to support nuclear mitochondrial gene expression through NRF-2/GABP, and biallelic variants were linked to intellectual disability and altered ACSF3 biochemistry (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35104841/). Its broad tissue expression (https://www.proteinatlas.org/ENSG00000066422-ZBTB11) made a narrowly mitochondrial effect plausible but did not predict the recurrent Rbm28-Stx16-Pigq branch.
support_and_caveats: Zbtb11 perturbation yielded 48 FDR-significant genes in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 17 in 191 MB P MY GABA, and 16 in 155 MB Glut. In 151 TH, Rbm28 decreased by log2FC -1.460 (FDR 3.57e-16), Stx16 by -1.320 (FDR 2.29e-14), Pigq by -1.260 (FDR 2.03e-13), and Acsf3 by -1.146 (FDR 7.68e-09); Stx16 also decreased in 155 MB Glut by -1.731 (FDR 1.50e-13), while Acsf3 and Ndufaf1 decreased in 191 MB P MY GABA by -1.897 (FDR 1.33e-06) and -2.459 (FDR 8.18e-04), respectively. The response burden covaries with perturbed-cell count, the relevant GABP partners were not perturbed, and RNA abundance alone cannot distinguish direct ZBTB11 targets from secondary mitochondrial or nucleolar stress.
research_community: Neurodevelopmental-disease, mitochondrial-gene-regulation, and nucleolar-stress researchers have the strongest reason to revise their models. Acute ZBTB11 protein depletion and rescue in matched neuronal cultures, measured alongside ZBTB11/GABP occupancy, nascent transcription, pre-rRNA synthesis, and respiration, would reveal whether the multi-compartment state begins with direct coordinated control or secondary stress. Early occupancy-linked effects would anchor a ZBTB11 disease program connecting genotype, ACSF3 metabolism, ribosome production, membrane trafficking, and circuit physiology.

finding_title: Arid1a, Smarcb1, Smarcc2, and Smarce1 perturbations converge on Ptpn3-Reep2-Prkcd repression with Clstn2-Nexn induction
core_idea: Within 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neurons, perturbing four BAF subunits repeatedly lowered Ptpn3, Reep2, Prkcd, Begain, and Lrrc7 while raising Clstn2 or Nexn; Arid1b and the SMARCA ATPase perturbations did not reproduce the corrected multi-gene pattern. One interpretation is dependence on a particular mature-neuronal cBAF/core configuration, although unequal functional disruption could also create the apparent subunit boundary.
significance: If the convergence reflects mature cBAF architecture, it would extend developmental BAF-switch models into maintenance of an adult neuronal identity and excitability program. That would create substantial follow-up directions for Coffin-Siris and related chromatin-remodeling disorders, including which subunits are mechanistically interchangeable after neuronal maturation and which outputs are reversible.
prior_expectation: Canonical cBAF-complex assembly (https://reactome.org/content/detail/R-HSA-9933937) places ARID1A, SMARCB1, SMARCC2, and SMARCE1 in related complexes, with ARID1A and ARID1B as alternative subunits. Neural BAF complexes were already known to undergo developmental subunit switching (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/17640523/) and to control dendritic programs in postmitotic neurons (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/17920018/). Some convergence was therefore expected, but the exact signed output and incomplete paralog phenocopy were not.
support_and_caveats: Under Arid1a perturbation in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Begain fell by log2FC -0.455 (FDR 4.82e-06), Kcnq2 by -0.219 (FDR 1.51e-04), Ptpn3 by -0.187 (FDR 0.00302), and Lrrc7 by -0.128 (FDR 0.00463), while Clstn2 rose by +0.385 (FDR 4.82e-06). Smarcb1 perturbation lowered Ptpn3 by -0.952 (FDR 1.30e-31), Reep2 by -0.610 (FDR 5.54e-26), and Prkcd by -0.537 (FDR 2.45e-12), while increasing Nexn by +0.652 (FDR 4.94e-09). Smarcc2 produced the same signs for Ptpn3 (-0.982, FDR 6.88e-24), Reep2 (-0.681, FDR 2.02e-20), Prkcd (-0.575, FDR 1.55e-10), and Nexn (+0.644, FDR 2.71e-06); Smarce1 likewise lowered Ptpn3 (-0.340, FDR 1.23e-07), Reep2 (-0.247, FDR 1.23e-07), and Prkcd (-0.357, FDR 6.58e-07). Arid1b and Smarca2 transcripts were significantly reduced yet the same marker panel was not FDR-supported, but protein loss and BAF occupancy were unmeasured, so this boundary cannot by itself prove true subunit dispensability. This matched within-context convergence is informative, but observing it only in high-yield 151 does not establish cell-type specificity.
research_community: Neuronal chromatin-remodeling, BAF-complex, and Coffin-Siris syndrome researchers would be most likely to change their working models. Matched acute degradation of each endogenous subunit in one mature thalamic model, followed by rescue, complex proteomics, chromatin accessibility, and occupancy at the Ptpn3/Reep2/Prkcd and Clstn2/Nexn loci, would separate complex-architecture dependence from unequal editing. A defined cBAF output module would underpin studies of mature-neuron complex composition, circuit excitability, disease-variant stratification, and postnatal reversibility.

finding_title: Ranbp2 perturbation produces Srrm2-down/Rbm15-up cortical and Grm1-Epha4-Itpr1-up cerebellar responses
core_idea: Ranbp2 perturbation produced a mixed RNA and nuclear-protein abundance response in 022 L5 ET CTX Glut neurons but a distinct Grm1-Epha4-Itpr1 calcium and synaptic induction in 308 CB GABA neurons. The cell-state interpretation is that the same RANBP2 nuclear-pore/SUMO lesion may be translated into different downstream liabilities by cortical projection neurons and cerebellar inhibitory neurons.
significance: A validated bifurcation would change RANBP2 models from a uniform nuclear-transport defect to a neuron-state-dependent mechanism with separable RNA and calcium consequences. It would create substantial opportunities to connect nuclear-pore SUMOylation to projection-neuron maintenance, cerebellar signaling, and the selective neurological manifestations of RANBP2 dysfunction.
prior_expectation: RANBP2 was already known as a nuclear-envelope component of the RanBP2–RanGAP1–SUMO1–Ubc9 complex (https://reactome.org/content/detail/R-HSA-3108232) with SUMO E3-ligase activity (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22464730/), so nuclear and RNA-related effects were plausible. A cerebellar calcium and synaptic induction was not an obvious generic consequence of that established function.
support_and_caveats: In 022 L5 ET CTX Glut, Ranbp2 itself decreased by log2FC -0.536 (FDR 0.00653), Gpr162 decreased by -0.487 (FDR 0.00778), Rbm15 increased by +0.751 (FDR 0.0194), and Srrm2 decreased by -0.373 (FDR 0.0350). In 308 CB GABA, Grm1 increased by +0.829 (FDR 0.00872), Epha4 by +1.084 (FDR 0.00872), and Itpr1 by +1.412 (FDR 0.0261). The two positive responses occur outside the highest-yield contexts, but the atlas measures RNA rather than SUMOylation, transport, or calcium physiology; unequal protein disruption or baseline state could therefore create two apparent branches without one common causal RANBP2 mechanism.
research_community: Nuclear-transport, SUMOylation, cortical-projection-neuron, and cerebellar-physiology researchers would be most affected. Matched acute RANBP2 protein depletion in L5 ET-like and cerebellar GABA neurons, with quantitative SUMO proteomics and transport assays in both and calcium imaging plus electrophysiology in the latter, would test for equal proximal disruption followed by divergent distal phenotypes. Such state-dependent decoding would motivate cell-class-specific models of RANBP2 circuit dysfunction and selective rescue.

finding_title: Rb1 and E2f4 perturbations release distinct replication and chromosome-repair arms in thalamic neurons
core_idea: In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neurons, Rb1 perturbation induced a Dnmt1-Tipin-Prim1-Lig1 DNA-replication arm, whereas E2f4 perturbation induced an Aaas-Rad18-Tacc3-Blm-Ddx11-Polq chromosome and repair arm. The observed separation supports a model in which postmitotic neurons retain distinct RB1-E2F and DREAM-E2F4 brakes, making ectopic cell-cycle transcription a set of replication-licensing and chromosome-maintenance routes rather than one undifferentiated re-entry program.
significance: Resolving these arms could materially sharpen models of abortive neuronal cell-cycle re-entry in degeneration and injury. It would support substantial work on which branch causes DNA damage, apoptosis, or survival and whether selective suppression of one arm can protect mature neurons without broadly blocking cell-cycle machinery elsewhere.
prior_expectation: Acute Rb inactivation was already known to trigger ectopic cell-cycle proteins and neuronal loss (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/23077065/), while RB–E2F and DREAM–E2F4 complexes were known to repress related but separable cell-cycle programs (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35835684/) and E2F4 was established as a p130–DREAM repressor component (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/17531812/). Thus derepression was expected, while the clean replication-versus-repair partition in this neuronal state was not.
support_and_caveats: After Rb1 perturbation in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Dnmt1 increased by log2FC +1.514 (FDR 9.33e-10), Tipin by +1.518 (FDR 2.93e-06), Prim1 by +2.724 (FDR 5.87e-05), and Lig1 by +1.942 (FDR 1.63e-04); Dnmt1 also rose in 155 MB Glut by +1.158 (FDR 7.69e-04). After E2f4 perturbation in 151 TH, Aaas increased by +1.331 (FDR 3.65e-14), Rad18 by +1.635 (FDR 5.31e-06), and Polq by +2.120 (FDR 0.00763). E2f1 and E2f5 did not reproduce these active states, but their negative comparisons do not establish functional equivalence of editing. Rb1 self-RNA was not FDR-reduced, and the assay does not measure RB1 protein, DREAM occupancy, DNA synthesis, DNA damage, apoptosis, or actual cell-cycle progression. The within-151 contrast is valid, but its high effective power precludes an inference that these arms are thalamus-specific.
research_community: Neuronal cell-cycle, DNA-damage, and neurodegeneration communities would be most motivated. Matched acute RB1 and E2F4 protein depletion in mature neurons should combine nascent RNA and RB/E2F4/p130 occupancy with EdU, replication-fork markers, DNA-damage imaging, and survival. Distinguishing transcriptional derepression from abortive S phase—and assigning different physiological outcomes to the two arms—would support branch-selective intervention across neurodegenerative and acute neuronal-injury models.

finding_title: Tardbp and Fus perturbations create opposite Snrnp70 responses within separable recurrent RNA-processing states
core_idea: Across 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA neurons, Tardbp perturbation recurrently induced Ppp6c, Fam135a, Gabpa, and Usp15 while lowering Snrnp70; Fus perturbation instead induced Rsrp1 and Atxn2l and raised Snrnp70. These opposing, recurrent observations support distinct acute TDP-43 and FUS RNA-processing abundance states rather than one generic ALS-gene stress response.
significance: The signed divergence offers a way to separate TDP-43 and FUS mechanisms in matched neurons and could yield state-specific biomarkers or modifiers for two major RNA-binding-protein disease axes. Because the signal recurs in several neuronal contexts, confirmation could sustain substantial programs on how shared RNA-processing machinery generates distinct downstream toxicity.
prior_expectation: TDP-43 was already established as a repressor of cryptic exons (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26250685/) with cell-type-dependent RNA targets (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28153034/), and FUS was known to bind brain RNAs and regulate alternative splicing (https://doi.org/10.1038/srep00603). These priors predicted RNA-processing defects but not the recurrent opposite Snrnp70 direction or the exact Tardbp-versus-Fus abundance programs.
support_and_caveats: In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Tardbp decreased by log2FC -1.414 (FDR 1.60e-39), while Ppp6c, Fam135a, and Gabpa increased by +1.985, +2.132, and +2.248 (FDR 2.45e-41, 4.16e-35, and 1.74e-38) and Snrnp70 decreased by -0.587 (FDR 5.10e-20). The signs recurred in 155 MB Glut for Ppp6c (+2.264, FDR 5.11e-30) and Snrnp70 (-0.667, FDR 2.80e-14), and in 191 MB P MY GABA for Ppp6c (+2.463, FDR 3.90e-17) and Snrnp70 (-0.589, FDR 1.53e-06). Fus perturbation in 151 TH lowered Fus by -1.407 (FDR 1.04e-45) but increased Rsrp1 by +0.428 (FDR 4.84e-29), Atxn2l by +0.411 (FDR 3.84e-14), and Snrnp70 by +0.261 (FDR 5.74e-05); Rsrp1 and Snrnp70 were also both positive in 155 MB and 191 MB. The 3-prime abundance assay cannot observe cryptic-exon inclusion, Stmn2 was not FDR-significant in the 151 Tardbp comparison, Unc13a abundance increased rather than recapitulating human cryptic-exon-associated depletion, and weak negative ALS comparators do not exclude their disease mechanisms.
research_community: ALS/FTD, RNA-splicing, and neuronal RNP communities would be most engaged. Isoform-resolved long-read or junction-level single-nucleus sequencing after matched acute TDP-43 and FUS depletion, combined with eCLIP and RNA-binding-mutant rescue, can separate direct isoform regulation from secondary abundance compensation at Snrnp70 and companion genes. Mechanistic separation would enable comparative biomarkers, modifier screens, and therapy testing tailored to TDP-43 versus FUS states.

finding_title: Proteasome-core and assembly perturbations couple proteasome-gene induction to loss of neuronal ion-pump and glutamate-receptor transcripts
core_idea: Perturbing Psmb4, Psmc1, Psmc5, or Pomp repeatedly increased proteasome or proteostasis transcripts while lowering Atp1a3, Atp1b1, or Gria2 in responsive midbrain glutamatergic, Pvalb, and hypothalamic GABA neurons. The interpretation is not that proteasome function was restored, but that compensatory transcription coexists with erosion of a mature-neuronal expression state.
significance: If the two arms are causally linked, proteasome stress in neurons is not adequately described by the familiar recovery response: the same cells may restore proteasome-component RNA while losing molecular support for membrane potential and glutamatergic signaling. That would justify a substantial program to define when proteasome compensation preserves neurons and when it marks entry into a physiologically compromised state relevant to neurodegeneration.
prior_expectation: Proteasome impairment was expected to engage recovery pathways because POMP was established as a proteasome-assembly factor (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/17948026/), neuronal loss of PSMC1 was known to cause proteasome failure and neurodegeneration (https://www.jneurosci.org/content/28/33/8189), and NFE2L1 had been shown to mediate proteasome recovery after inhibition (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/20385086/). Those sources do not predict the accompanying loss of ion-pump and glutamate-receptor RNA.
support_and_caveats: In 155 MB Glut, Pomp perturbation lowered Atp1a3 (log2FC -1.075, FDR 2.98e-11) and Gria2 (-0.997, FDR 1.16e-6) while increasing Ddit3 (+1.674, FDR 3.04e-5) and Psmc5 (+0.530, FDR 0.00268). In the same class, Psmc1 perturbation lowered Atp1a3 (-1.432, FDR 1.62e-23) and Atp1b1 (-1.556, FDR 1.98e-25), increased Ddit3 (+2.122, FDR 1.32e-9) and Psmd4 (+0.921, FDR 1.01e-7); Psmc5 perturbation likewise lowered Atp1a3 (-1.247, FDR 8.07e-13) and Atp1b1 (-1.094, FDR 1.78e-8) while increasing Psma5 (+0.891, FDR 0.00244). In 052 Pvalb Gaba, Psmb4 perturbation lowered Atp1a3 (-1.001, FDR 3.49e-4) and Gria2 (-0.886, FDR 1.20e-5) while increasing Psmc6 (+0.766, FDR 2.39e-6), Psmd4 (+0.960, FDR 5.34e-5), and Psme4 (+0.713, FDR 2.28e-4); the same directions recurred in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA. The principal limitation is that RNA abundance does not measure proteasome activity, recovery, neuronal firing, or survival; shared integrated stress or a general state shift could generate both arms, and functional editing was not independently quantified.
research_community: Neuronal proteostasis, proteasome-recovery, and neurodegeneration researchers need to distinguish compensatory RNA induction from physiological rescue. Matched editing of several proteasome nodes in defined neurons, with proteasome-activity reporters, longitudinal survival, and patch-clamp measurement of Na+/K+-pump and glutamatergic function, would reveal whether recovery-gene induction can be uncoupled from decline. That distinction could guide a subunit-by-neuron vulnerability program and interventions that preserve excitability during proteasome stress.

finding_title: ANK3 perturbation lowers calcium-handling, receptor, and active-zone transcripts without a matched Cntn1, Cntnap1, or Sptan1 response
core_idea: ANK3-targeted thalamic Prkcd/Grin2c glutamatergic neurons lost a broad set of calcium-handling, synaptic, and receptor transcripts, whereas targeting the nodal or cytoskeletal partners Cntn1, Cntnap1, and Sptan1 did not reproduce that RNA state in the same context. This matched observation supports, without proving, a model in which ankyrin-G maintains a transcriptionally coupled excitability program beyond generic node or axon-initial-segment structural disruption.
significance: A validated scaffold-to-transcription connection would extend ankyrin-G biology from channel localization to maintenance of the molecular state that supports synaptic and calcium physiology. Because ANK3 is central to neuronal excitability and psychiatric genetics, separating this program from general axonal-structure failure could motivate multiple studies of how membrane scaffolds communicate with the nucleus.
prior_expectation: Established work predicted that ankyrin-G organizes axon-initial-segment and nodal membrane domains (https://doi.org/10.1083/jcb.200612012), while SPTAN1 studies defined an ankyrin–spectrin assembly hierarchy (https://www.jneurosci.org/content/37/47/11311) and linked spectrin dysfunction to neurological disease (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36697767/). It did not specifically predict coordinated regulation of Atp2a2, Atp2b1, Erc2, Vgf, and neurotransmitter-receptor transcripts.
support_and_caveats: In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Ank3 perturbation lowered Ank3 itself (log2FC -0.256, FDR 8.42e-5), Opn3 (-1.053, FDR 9.24e-11), Atp2a2 (-0.360, FDR 9.24e-11), Atp2b1 (-0.337, FDR 3.81e-10), Erc2 (-0.545, FDR 1.75e-8), Vgf (-0.852, FDR 2.40e-8), Ache (-0.688, FDR 2.58e-8), Cacna2d1 (-0.227, FDR 0.00184), Gabra4 (-0.191, FDR 0.00226), Grm1 (-0.214, FDR 0.00770), and Gria4 (-0.205, FDR 0.0167), while increasing Pcsk1n (+0.552, FDR 1.10e-8). Cntn1, Cntnap1, and Sptan1 were each strongly depleted in the same class (respectively log2FC -0.880, -0.822, and -0.529; FDR 4.36e-29, 1.09e-11, and 2.03e-13), yet their Atp2a2, Opn3, Atp2b1, Pcsk1n, and Erc2 rows all had FDR 1.0. The alternative is unequal functional editing, protein turnover, or a perturbation-specific stress response rather than an ankyrin-G-to-nucleus pathway; axon-initial-segment structure and electrical function were not measured, and the positive state was resolved in one high-yield context.
research_community: Axon-initial-segment, ankyrin/spectrin, ion-channel, and psychiatric-neurogenetics communities would be most affected. ANK3 and structural comparators should be depleted to matched protein levels, then ANK3 rescued with constructs that retain or lack defined channel/scaffold-binding domains while axon-initial-segment architecture, nascent RNA, and excitability are measured. Domain-selective transcript rescue would distinguish signaling from generic structural injury and connect ANK3 risk alleles to scaffold-dependent transcriptional homeostasis.

finding_title: ADARB1 perturbation recurrently lowers Flnb across cortical, subcortical, and cerebellar neuronal classes
core_idea: Flnb RNA decreased directionally after Adarb1 perturbation in every tested neuronal class and reached FDR significance in 12 of 22, with large effects across thalamic, midbrain, hypothalamic, Pvalb, cortical, and cerebellar populations. Flnb is therefore a robust neuronal readout of ADAR2 loss, but its interpretation remains open among FLNB editing, another ADAR2-dependent RNA process, and an indirect cytoskeletal-state response.
significance: The result redirects attention from canonical glutamate-receptor substrates toward a recurrent filamin/actin-associated consequence of ADAR2 disruption. If the ADARB1-FLNB connection proves causal, RNA-editing researchers could pursue a new route by which ADAR2 influences neuronal structure, mechanics, or transport, with implications for disease phenotypes not explained by GRIA2 alone.
prior_expectation: ADAR2 was already known to edit Q/R sites in FLNA and FLNB, and a study of ADAR2-deficient mouse heart (https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0200968) examined FLNB editing and expression. That precedent makes a filamin connection biologically plausible, but it did not establish a recurrent neuronal Flnb-abundance decrease across these brain populations.
support_and_caveats: Adarb1 perturbation lowered Flnb in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut (log2FC -1.479, FDR 6.67e-44), 155 MB Glut (-1.654, FDR 1.57e-38), 191 MB P MY GABA (-1.477, FDR 7.81e-16), 145 MH-LH TH Glut (-1.198, FDR 6.89e-15), 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA (-0.913, FDR 6.36e-11), and 052 Pvalb Gaba (-0.797, FDR 2.44e-8). Additional significant decreases occurred in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut (-0.693, FDR 2.52e-5), 054 CNU-MGE GABA (-0.850, FDR 1.38e-4), 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut (-0.912, FDR 1.57e-4), 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut (-0.890, FDR 0.0276), and 308 CB GABA (-0.738, FDR 0.0218). Adarb1 itself was depleted in 151 (-0.555, FDR 2.04e-9), 066 (-0.816, FDR 0.0189), and 052 (-0.616, FDR 0.0401). The strongest alternative is an editing-dependent effect on FLNB RNA stability rather than an editing-independent regulatory link; editing sites, FLNB protein, cytoskeletal function, and matched Adar or Gria2 functional engagement were not measured.
research_community: RNA-editing, neuronal-cytoskeleton, and ADAR-linked-disease communities would gain a common mechanistic question. Targeted long-read RNA sequencing and site-resolved editing after ADARB1 loss, with wild-type versus catalytically inactive ADAR2 rescue and editing-mimetic FLNB constructs, can separate editing-dependent transcript stability from indirect or editing-independent regulation. The answer would support systematic mapping from ADAR2-dependent structural RNA targets to neuronal morphology and circuit phenotypes.

finding_title: MAX perturbation derepresses STAG3 and circadian E-box genes while MGA shares only the STAG3 branch
core_idea: MAX targeting strongly induced Stag3 in thalamic and midbrain glutamatergic neurons and induced Per2 and Cry1 in the thalamic class; MGA targeting also induced Stag3 and Obscn but shared little whole-transcriptome similarity with MAX. The pattern suggests separable MAX-containing repressor branches in adult neurons—an MGA-associated germline/meiotic branch and a distinct circadian E-box branch—rather than a unitary loss of MYC-driven biosynthesis.
significance: Confirming separable MAX repressor outputs would revise how the MYC/MAX network is organized in mature neurons and connect chromatin repression of normally silent meiotic genes to neuronal clock control. It would support substantial work on how different MAX partners partition repression, whether inappropriate germline-gene activation harms neurons, and whether clock disruption is mechanistically linked or parallel.
prior_expectation: MAX is the shared bHLHZip partner for activating MYC complexes and several repressive MXD/MNT/MGA complexes. Prior work supports MAX/MGA repression of germline genes (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29381691/) and meiotic genes (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/27025988/), as well as MAX-dependent repression at circadian E-box promoters (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32225100/). The unexpected feature is that these branches separate within the same neuronal perturbation map rather than moving as one generic MAX program.
support_and_caveats: In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Max perturbation increased Stag3 (log2FC +3.324, FDR 1.90e-11), Per2 (+1.108, FDR 1.64e-10), and Cry1 (+0.654, FDR 0.0275); in 155 MB Glut it increased Stag3 (+3.047, FDR 5.03e-6). Mga perturbation in 151 increased Stag3 (+3.606, FDR 4.83e-5) and Obscn (+4.435, FDR 1.73e-8). The source found 167 FDR-significant Max gene-by-cell rows across six tested contexts, but MAX and MGA had weak whole-transcriptome similarity. Max RNA itself was not FDR-depleted and had mixed directions, so the result is a Max-locus perturbation phenotype, not demonstrated MAX protein loss. The reported absence of Stag3 induction after MYC/MYCN/E2F-DP targeting is not decisive without matched functional engagement, and direct occupancy or ncPRC1.6 activity was not measured. Concentration of the strongest positive rows in 151/155 is compatible with their high effective power and does not establish restriction to those classes.
research_community: MYC/MAX-network, ncPRC1.6, neuronal-chromatin, and circadian-transcription researchers need to determine whether the two branches occupy distinct regulatory complexes. Time-resolved MAX and MGA CUT&RUN with nascent RNA after independently validated editing would test direct, partner-specific control at Stag3 and Per2/Cry1. Separating those branches would motivate substantial work on mature-neuron repressor-complex partitioning, ectopic germline programs, and clock-linked vulnerability.

finding_title: GRIN2A raises an L2/3 NPTX2-BDNF-PTGS2 program while GRIN2B trends oppositely and significantly lowers Vgf and Kcnv1
core_idea: GRIN2A targeting increased an activity/plasticity-associated RNA set in upper-layer cortical excitatory neurons, whereas GRIN2B targeting in L2/3 moved the same markers downward, with FDR support strongest for Vgf and Kcnv1 on the GRIN2B side. Opposite homeostatic states after chronic loss of GluN2A- and GluN2B-containing receptors are a plausible interpretation, but asymmetry in statistical and on-target support makes subunit non-equivalence provisional.
significance: Validated sign-opposed responses would add a chronic transcriptional dimension to GluN2A/GluN2B specialization and could change how subunit-selective NMDAR interventions are expected to remodel cortical circuits over time. This would seed work connecting receptor composition to homeostatic plasticity, neurotrophin signaling, and long-term drug effects rather than treating both subunits as interchangeable reductions in NMDAR current.
prior_expectation: Established work predicted distinct GluN2A and GluN2B disease and circuit roles (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/31807283/), while NPTX2/Narp homeostatic synaptic scaling (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/20729843/) and NMDA-receptor-dependent neuronal PTGS2 induction (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35354047/) provided marker-level precedents. It did not specifically predict opposite chronic regulation of the Nptx2/Bdnf/Ptgs2/Vgf group in superficial cortical neurons.
support_and_caveats: In 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut, Grin2a perturbation increased Nptx2 (log2FC +1.777, FDR 6.09e-4), Bdnf (+1.249, FDR 0.0272), Ptgs2 (+1.264, FDR 0.0353), and Cckbr (+0.832, FDR 0.00117); Vgf also rose (+0.650) but had FDR 0.395. In 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, the most secure component was Nptx2 induction (+1.401, FDR 7.94e-6), with Grin2a depletion at -0.349, FDR 0.0239. In 007, Grin2b perturbation depleted Grin2b (-0.471, FDR 0.00107), lowered Kcnv1 (-1.108, FDR 2.89e-5) and Vgf (-0.987, FDR 0.0194), and moved Bdnf (-1.156, FDR 0.184), Cckbr (-0.831, FDR 0.0707), Nptx2 (-1.032, FDR 0.617), and Ptgs2 (-1.453, FDR 0.286) in the opposite direction without FDR support. Thus the multigene reversal rests partly on nominal evidence, and Grin2a itself was not FDR-depleted in L2/3 (log2FC -0.401, FDR 0.274). Unequal editing, receptor turnover, baseline activity, or sampled cell state could explain the contrast; receptor currents and network activity were not measured.
research_community: NMDAR-subunit, cortical-plasticity, and neuropsychiatric-pharmacology communities would be most motivated by a verified sign reversal. Independently validated, matched Grin2a and Grin2b edits in identified L2/3 neurons should be followed longitudinally through subunit currents, network activity, and RNA trajectories, with subunit-specific rescue as the causal test. Reversible divergence would create a research direction on chronic subunit-selective homeostasis and delayed responses to NMDAR-modulating drugs.

finding_title: EEF2 targeting induces a large Vgf, Nptx2, and Cx3cl1 trophic state in superficial cortical neurons
core_idea: EEF2 targeting generated a 575-gene response in L2/3 intratelencephalic cortical neurons, led by strong Vgf, Nptx2, and Cx3cl1 induction and Uchl1 repression, with smaller Vgf- or Ranbp2-positive responses in other neuronal classes. Impaired elongation may provoke a superficial-cortical trophic and neuron-to-glia signaling state, but unchanged Eef2 RNA and the absence of direct translation measurements leave guide-linked or secondary state effects unresolved.
significance: If EEF2 protein disruption causes this state, translational stress in cortical neurons would have an unexpectedly strong secretory and trophic output rather than a simple uniform loss of protein synthesis. That could support major work on how vulnerable excitatory neurons signal adaptation or distress to surrounding cells and whether VGF, NPTX2, or CX3CL1 promotes recovery versus pathology.
prior_expectation: EEF2 is the conserved ribosomal translocation factor (https://rest.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P58252), and neuronal eEF2 phosphorylation is established as a regulator of dendritic translation (https://doi.org/10.3389/fncel.2014.00035). These priors predict translation-related consequences but not a large Vgf/Nptx2/Cx3cl1 abundance state centered in superficial cortical neurons.
support_and_caveats: In 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut, Eef2 perturbation increased Vgf (log2FC +2.149, FDR 1.01e-8), Nptx2 (+2.946, FDR 3.02e-8), and Cx3cl1 (+0.864, FDR 4.93e-8), while lowering Uchl1 (-0.712, FDR 5.35e-5); the full response contained 575 FDR-significant genes. Smaller echoes included Vgf induction in 052 Pvalb Gaba (+1.424, FDR 1.35e-5) and Ranbp2 induction in 155 MB Glut (+0.827, FDR 2.60e-5). Eef2 RNA itself was not FDR-depleted in any tested class, and effective protein disruption, elongation rate, ribosome occupancy, cell survival, and secreted peptide levels were not measured. Independent-guide effects, selective survival, or a pre-existing state imbalance are therefore major alternatives, and the stronger L2/3 yield does not by itself establish intrinsic cell-type specificity.
research_community: Translation-control, cortical-circuit, neurotrophin, and neuron-glia-signaling researchers would pursue whether this trophic state is adaptive. Independent Eef2 alleles, protein quantification, ribosome profiling or nascent-protein labeling, and time-resolved single-cell RNA would first distinguish elongation stress from guide-linked selection; VGF/CX3CL1 neutralization could then test effects on edited and neighboring cells. Those results would support a program on secretory adaptation to translational stress across cortical layers and disease models.

finding_title: BRAF and MAP2K1 perturbations repress, whereas NF1 perturbation induces, a neuronal VGF-PTPN5-ETV5 MAPK module
core_idea: In thalamic Prkcd/Grin2c glutamatergic neurons, BRAF and MAP2K1 targeting lowered a shared Vgf/Ptpn5/Unc13a axis, NF1 targeting moved Vgf, Ptpn5, Atp2a2, and Etv5 upward, and SHOC2 targeting also lowered Vgf; NF1-associated Vgf induction recurred in midbrain glutamatergic and midbrain/pons/myelencephalon GABA neurons. These signed RNA responses support a neuronal RAF-MEK branch opposite the NF1 Ras brake, while weaker paralog and LZTR1 comparisons remain boundaries rather than evidence of biochemical dispensability.
significance: The expected pathway polarity becomes valuable here because it is attached to a concrete neuronal output containing VGF, STEP/PTPN5, ETV factors, calcium handling, and release machinery. Validating that output could give RASopathy and neurofibromatosis research a cell-resolved bridge from pathway genotype to neuronal physiology and enable branch-selective biomarkers for interventions.
prior_expectation: BRAF is an upstream kinase for MAP2K1 and MAPK activation (https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P15056/entry). NF1 is a Ras GTPase-activating negative regulator whose loss activates the RAS/RAF/MAPK pathway (https://reactome.org/content/detail/R-HSA-6802957), whereas SHOC2 supports RAF activation dynamics (https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.1902658116). The expected sign is therefore NF1 loss opposite BRAF/MEK loss; the new element is the specific mature-neuronal RNA module and its recurrence.
support_and_caveats: In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Map2k1 perturbation lowered Vgf (log2FC -0.785, FDR 7.85e-8), Ptpn5 (-0.436, FDR 9.37e-4), Unc13a (-0.325, FDR 0.0119), and Etv5 (-0.631, FDR 0.0119). Braf perturbation lowered Vgf (-0.795, FDR 1.39e-4), Ptpn5 (-0.635, FDR 1.39e-4), Atp2a2 (-0.263, FDR 1.39e-4), and Unc13a (-0.315, FDR 0.00393). Nf1 perturbation reversed the axis: Vgf +0.848 (FDR 1.36e-11), Ptpn5 +0.550 (FDR 1.64e-8), Atp2a2 +0.260 (FDR 7.30e-5), and Etv5 +0.541 (FDR 0.0127); Shoc2 perturbation lowered Vgf (-0.660, FDR 0.00794). NF1-associated Vgf induction recurred in 155 MB Glut (+2.192, FDR 1.75e-16) and 191 MB P MY GABA (+1.871, FDR 1.78e-9), where Scg2 and Unc13a also rose (+0.856 and +0.482, both FDR 0.00820). Braf RNA depletion was not FDR-significant, Map2k1 self-depletion was not FDR-significant, and direct MAPK phosphorylation or activity was not measured; differential editing, activity-state changes, and Vgf neurotrophin responsiveness could explain part of the polarity. Nominal LZTR1 rows and weak RAF1/MAPK1 negatives do not establish node-specific independence.
research_community: RASopathy, neurofibromatosis, neuronal-MAPK, and synaptic-plasticity communities could use this as a candidate functional map of pathway dosage. A matched NF1, BRAF, MAP2K1, and SHOC2 allelic series in identified neuronal classes, with time-resolved phospho-ERK and genetic epistasis, should test whether ERK normalization restores VGF/PTPN5/ETV5 and electrical phenotypes in the predicted order. Causal ordering would support stratification of RAS/MAPK disorders by neuronal branch output and tests of state-selective pathway correction.

finding_title: SIN3A targeting induces cilium and cholesterol genes while repressing spliceosome transcripts in thalamic and midbrain neurons
core_idea: SIN3A targeting produced a large thalamic response with induction of cilium/centrosome, Hcn3, Cyp46a1, and Grn transcripts alongside repression of Srrm2, Snrnp70, Rnpc3, Ddx17, and other RNA-processing genes; a smaller cilium/cholesterol and spliceosome pattern recurred in midbrain and inhibitory neurons. A SIN3A-dependent chromatin state coordinating ciliary or sterol biology with RNA processing is one interpretation, but the upward Sin3a RNA shift and response breadth leave direct repression, allelic consequence, and causal unity unresolved.
significance: SIN3A-related disease is usually framed through cortical development and intellectual disability. A validated mature-neuronal program joining cilia, brain cholesterol turnover, and spliceosome abundance would broaden that model and create several mechanistically linked directions for Witteveen-Kolk syndrome, synaptic plasticity, and neuronal chromatin research.
prior_expectation: SIN3A was expected to act as an HDAC-associated transcriptional scaffold (https://doi.org/10.1016/j.bbagrm.2009.05.007), and haploinsufficiency is established in a neurodevelopmental syndrome with altered cortical development (https://doi.org/10.1038/ng.3619). Postnatal excitatory-neuron deletion also affects hippocampal plasticity through Homer1/mGluR5 signaling (https://doi.org/10.1172/jci.insight.92385). These sources do not predict the observed cilium/cholesterol-plus-spliceosome relationship.
support_and_caveats: In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Sin3a targeting increased Odf2 (log2FC +0.820, FDR 1.71e-26), Hcn3 (+2.192, FDR 3.99e-23), Dzip1 (+0.840, FDR 4.54e-21), Cyp46a1 (+0.299, FDR 1.30e-10), and Grn (+0.423, FDR 0.00419), while lowering Srrm2 (-0.476, FDR 1.60e-19), Snhg11 (-0.236, FDR 5.84e-19), Snrnp70 (-0.392, FDR 2.39e-11), Rnpc3 (-0.593, FDR 2.76e-11), and Ddx17 (-0.352, FDR 1.05e-9). In 155 MB Glut, the grounded summary reports Cyp46a1 induction with score 7.553 and FDR 1.85e-10, Odf2 induction with score 7.119 and FDR 2.70e-9, Snhg11 repression with score -9.925 and FDR 5.67e-19, and Srrm2 repression with score -7.924 and FDR 1.34e-11. Sin3a RNA itself increased in 151 (+1.354, FDR 2.36e-17) and in four other responsive classes, so its direction cannot be read as measured loss; protein disruption, chromatin occupancy, splicing, ciliary structure, cholesterol flux, and neuronal physiology were not assessed. A broad stress response or guide-specific allele effect could unite the signatures, and weak REST or other chromatin-comparator responses do not prove SIN3A specificity. The dominance of 151/155 may reflect their greater effective power, so it cannot establish preferential biological sensitivity.
research_community: SIN3A/Witteveen-Kolk, neuronal-chromatin, cilia, cholesterol, and RNA-processing communities need to determine whether this is one regulatory state or several secondary consequences. Defined Sin3a alleles with SIN3A protein quantification, CUT&RUN/ATAC, and long-read RNA in the same purified neurons would test direct occupancy and splicing, while ciliary imaging and sterol measurements separate downstream branches. Coherent causal ordering would establish a mature-neuron SIN3A program connecting chromatin dosage to organelle, lipid, and RNA-processing phenotypes.

finding_title: KMT2A perturbation reveals a mature thalamic Nr2f1-Pcdh7-Lhx9 maintenance state
core_idea: Observation: Kmt2a perturbation lowered Nr2f1, Pcdh7, Lhx9, Camk2d, Pcdh10, and Grik2 and increased Igfbp5 and Cx3cl1 in thalamic neurons, while other neuronal classes showed only singletons or a tiny midbrain branch. Interpretation: acute KMT2A loss in mature neurons engages a defined thalamic maintenance regulon rather than a broad developmental HOX or neurogenesis program.
significance: The result extends KMT2A biology from development and memory into a specific mature-neuronal expression state. Its scope is moderate because direct chromatin regulation and physiological consequence remain to be demonstrated.
prior_expectation: Neuronal KMT2A was already required for prefrontal plasticity and working memory (Jakovcevski et al. 2015 (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25834037/)), postnatal neural-stem-cell neurogenesis and Dlx2 activation (Lim et al. 2009 (https://doi.org/10.1038/nature07726)), and human KMT2A mutations cause Wiedemann-Steiner syndrome (Jones et al. 2012 (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22795537/)). The atlas adds a postmitotic thalamic output distinct from those known settings.
support_and_caveats: In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Kmt2a perturbation lowered Nr2f1 (log2FC -0.806, FDR 2.39e-10), Pcdh7 (-0.774, FDR 3.60e-7), Lhx9 (-1.182, FDR 1.54e-4), and Kmt2a (-0.485, FDR 1.76e-4), while increasing Igfbp5 (+0.874, FDR 0.0126); 24 genes passed FDR<0.05. In 155 MB Glut, Fnbp1l (-0.749, FDR 0.0214) and Kmt2a were the only FDR rows, and three additional glutamatergic classes yielded isolated Ptprk, Aff4, or Nap1l2 hits. Las1l did not phenocopy Kmt2a, but most other 5FMC components were not perturbed, so complex-level exclusion is incomplete. KMT2A protein, H3K4 methylation, occupancy, and neuronal function were not measured.
research_community: KMT2A/Wiedemann-Steiner, neuronal chromatin, and thalamic-development researchers would be most interested. Matched acute KMT2A loss with CUT&RUN, H3K4 profiling, nascent RNA, and rescue by catalytic versus scaffold mutants would distinguish direct mature-neuronal targets from secondary state change. Confirmation would support a focused program on postmitotic KMT2A maintenance rather than broad developmental reanalysis.

finding_title: YLPM1 perturbation lowers Srsf6-Srsf5 and Inha in midbrain-linked neurons
core_idea: Observation: Ylpm1 RNA was reduced across several neuronal classes, but midbrain glutamatergic neurons additionally lowered Srsf6, Srsf5, and Inha, with Inha recurring in posterior GABAergic neurons. Interpretation: YLPM1 loss may stress nuclear-speckle or post-transcriptional machinery in these neurons, although the branch is primarily supported by one high-yield midbrain context.
significance: The result supplies a concrete neuronal output for a poorly characterized nuclear protein and a small set of markers for mechanistic follow-up. It is likely to extend RNA-processing work rather than establish a broad new disease program.
prior_expectation: YLPM1 was annotated as a nuclear protein associated with speckle-related compartments (UniProt YLPM1 (https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/Q9R0I7); Human Protein Atlas (https://www.proteinatlas.org/ENSG00000119596-YLPM1)), and nuclear speckles are defined by RNA-processing factors (QuickGO GO:0016607 (https://www.ebi.ac.uk/QuickGO/term/GO:0016607)). These priors make SRSF changes plausible but do not predict their neuronal context.
support_and_caveats: In 155 MB Glut, Ylpm1 perturbation lowered Ylpm1 (log2FC -0.652, FDR 6.93e-4), Srsf6 (-0.610, FDR 9.35e-4), Srsf5 (-0.440, FDR 0.00429), and Inha (-0.501, FDR 0.0232), while increasing Shprh (+0.787, FDR 9.35e-4), Jakmip2 (+0.875, FDR 0.0231), and Atxn2l (+0.362, FDR 0.0232). In 191 MB P MY GABA, Ylpm1 and Inha both fell about -0.833 (FDR 5.92e-4). Ylpm1 also fell in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA (-1.173, FDR 7.09e-4) without a broad companion program. The latter null does not prove state-selective coupling because effective power and protein loss were unmeasured; speckle morphology, splice isoforms, and direct YLPM1 interactions were not assayed.
research_community: Nuclear-speckle, splice-regulator, and YLPM1 rare-disease researchers would be the relevant audience. Imaging speckle organization and long-read RNA after matched YLPM1 protein depletion in midbrain and comparator neurons, followed by YLPM1 rescue, would test whether the SRSF changes report genuine speckle dysfunction. Confirmation would support a bounded mechanistic study of YLPM1-dependent RNA processing.

finding_title: BMAL1-CLOCK and REV-ERB perturbations recover an asymmetric neuronal circadian feedback loop
core_idea: Observation: Bmal1 and Clock perturbations lowered Dbp, Nr1d2, and related clock outputs, whereas Nr1d1 or Nr1d2 perturbations induced portions of the positive clock limb and a synaptic branch in thalamic neurons. Interpretation: the atlas recovers expected circadian feedback but shows asymmetric paralog and endpoint behavior that should be treated as a single-timepoint basal state, not a phase-resolved oscillator.
significance: The finding validates that pooled postnatal perturbation can recover a neuronal clock circuit and identifies a tractable thalamic synaptic output. Its priority is moderate because the central feedback logic is established and the experiment lacks time resolution.
prior_expectation: CLOCK:BMAL1 activation of core clock genes and the PER/CRY and REV-ERB feedback loops are established (Reactome circadian clock (https://reactome.org/content/detail/R-HSA-9909396); Trott and Menet 2018 (https://journals.plos.org/plosgenetics/article?id=10.1371/journal.pgen.1007156)), and REV-ERB paralogs are known to coordinate circadian output (Ikeda et al. 2019 (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6629614/)). The atlas primarily adds neuronal context and signed asymmetry.
support_and_caveats: In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Bmal1 perturbation lowered Dbp (log2FC -1.601, FDR 3.07e-22), Nr1d2 (-1.083, FDR 1.19e-18), and Nr1d1 (-1.074, FDR 4.70e-18), while increasing Erc2 (+0.628, FDR 1.32e-12); 103 genes passed FDR<0.05. Clock perturbation in the same class lowered Dbp -1.030 (FDR 1.36e-11) and Nr1d2 -0.378 (FDR 2.25e-4), and in 155 MB Glut lowered Nr1d2 -0.833 (FDR 1.30e-13) and Dbp -1.290 (FDR 2.05e-6). Nr1d2 perturbation increased Nr1d1 +0.520 in 151 (FDR 1.44e-5), while Nr1d1 perturbation increased Dbp +0.407 (FDR 0.00243) and generated a 116-gene branch. A single harvest time can invert or attenuate feedback depending on phase, and neither circadian period nor rhythmic amplitude was measured.
research_community: Circadian-neurobiology and thalamic-circuit researchers would use the result mainly as a starting map. Time-resolved perturbation across circadian phase, with bioluminescent clock reporters and electrophysiology, would distinguish altered oscillator dynamics from static phase displacement. Confirmation would support a focused program on how the neuronal clock gates synaptic-state genes in defined thalamic cells.

finding_title: HSPA8 perturbation induces a compact HSP70-HSP90 compensatory transcript arm
core_idea: Observation: Hspa8 perturbation increased Dnaja1, Hspa4l, Hsp90aa1, and Cct6a in thalamic neurons, with Dnaja1 or Hsp90aa1 induction recurring in cortical and hypothalamic classes. Interpretation: loss of constitutive HSPA8 releases a compensatory folding response, although correlation with proteasome perturbations does not prove altered folding flux.
significance: The response gives a concise neuronal measure of HSPA8 insufficiency and supports comparison of constitutive versus inducible chaperone networks. It is a well-grounded extension of established feedback biology with moderate experimental value.
prior_expectation: HSPA8 was established as a constitutive HSP70 chaperone (UniProt HSPA8 (https://rest.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P11142)), DNAJ proteins as HSP70 specificity factors (Kampinga and Craig 2010 (https://doi.org/10.1038/nrm2941)), and HSP70–HSF1 negative feedback as a mechanism for compensatory chaperone induction (Krakowiak et al. 2018 (https://doi.org/10.7554/eLife.31668)). The observed arm therefore has strong precedent.
support_and_caveats: In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Hspa8 perturbation increased Dnaja1 (log2FC +0.496, FDR 7.23e-4), Hspa4l (+0.394, FDR 7.23e-4), Hsp90aa1 (+0.383, FDR 0.00252), and Cct6a (+0.700, FDR 0.0203). Dnaja1 also increased in 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut (+0.581, FDR 0.0196), and Hsp90aa1 increased in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA (+0.720, FDR 0.0198). Nominal positive calls for Hsph1, Dnaja1, Dnajb1, Hsp90aa1, Stip1, and Hspa4l recurred across the 21 tested classes. Protein folding, HSF1 activity, aggregation, and proteasome flux were not measured, so the interpretation remains an abundance-level compensatory response rather than demonstrated proteostasis recovery.
research_community: Neuronal proteostasis, HSP70/HSP90, and chaperone-therapy researchers would find the marker arm useful. HSF1 reporter assays, folding sensors, proteomics, and wild-type versus ATPase-deficient HSPA8 rescue would determine whether transcript induction restores functional proteostasis. Confirmation would support a focused neuronal chaperone-feedback study rather than a broad new program.

finding_title: PPP3CA and PPP3R1 perturbations expose a noncanonical calcineurin transcript output opposite AP-2 adaptor states
core_idea: Observation: Ppp3ca and Ppp3r1 perturbations produced compact, partially overlapping thalamic responses centered on Pcsk1n and selected calcium, synaptic, and receptor genes, while AP-2 adaptor perturbations moved the restricted Ppp3r1 signature oppositely. Interpretation: calcineurin loss is captured here by an endocytic and excitability-related RNA module rather than a canonical NFAT/RCAN abundance reporter.
significance: The response suggests a tractable transcriptional interface between calcineurin and synaptic endocytosis, but it does not yet establish phosphatase-to-AP-2 epistasis. It is a moderate-priority refinement of well-known calcineurin biology.
prior_expectation: Calcineurin was already established as a calcium-dependent phosphatase that activates NFAT (Reactome (https://reactome.org/content/detail/R-HSA-2025928)) and dephosphorylates endocytic proteins during synaptic-vesicle recycling (Cousin and Robinson 2001 (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/11672811/)). Those priors make both NFAT and endocytic outputs plausible; the atlas instead emphasizes a compact non-NFAT RNA state.
support_and_caveats: In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Ppp3ca perturbation lowered Ppp3ca (log2FC -0.483, FDR 6.35e-12) and Iyd (-1.085, FDR 0.0112) while changing Ptpn3 (-0.224, FDR 0.0239) and Pik3r1 (+0.488, FDR 0.0239). Ppp3r1 perturbation lowered Ppp3r1 (-0.703, FDR 1.89e-5), Atp2a2 (-0.327, FDR 8.08e-5), Coro6 (-0.472, FDR 5.99e-4), and Slc6a17 (-0.286, FDR 0.0496), while increasing Pcsk1n (+0.710, FDR 2.21e-7) and Ptprs (+0.356, FDR 4.87e-7). Ap2s1 and Ap2m1 were the strongest negative signature neighbors; for example, Ap2s1 perturbation increased Atp2a2 and Slc6a17 while lowering Ptprs and Ndrg2. That anticorrelation is not double-perturbation epistasis, and NFAT localization, phosphatase activity, endocytosis, and calcium were not measured.
research_community: Calcineurin, synaptic-vesicle endocytosis, and calcium-signaling researchers would be most interested. Matched calcineurin-subunit and AP-2 perturbations with phosphatase assays, endocytic imaging, NFAT localization, and double-perturbation rescue would distinguish a causal countermodule from correlated neuronal states. Confirmation would support a focused study of calcineurin–endocytosis coupling in mature thalamic neurons.

finding_title: ACTB perturbation recurrently induces ACTG1 and FLNA without reciprocal ACTG1 compensation
core_idea: Observation: Actb perturbation increased Actg1 and Flna across multiple neuronal classes, whereas Actg1 perturbation did not produce a broad reciprocal Actb-like state and yielded only a narrow Flna response. Interpretation: cytoplasmic actin compensation is directionally asymmetric and includes a filamin-associated remodeling arm.
significance: The pattern gives neuronal context to established β- versus γ-actin nonredundancy and could help interpret cytoskeletal disease alleles. It is robust but closely aligned with known actin biology, so follow-up should remain proportionate.
prior_expectation: β- and γ-cytoplasmic actins were already known to encode nearly identical proteins with nonredundant gene-level functions (Vedula et al. 2017 (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29244021/); Patrinostro et al. 2018 (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30012594/)), and ACTB/ACTG1 variants cause a shared developmental syndrome (Rivière et al. 2012 (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22366783/)). Asymmetric compensation was therefore plausible.
support_and_caveats: After Actb perturbation, Actg1 increased in 9 of 22 contexts and Flna in 13 of 22 at FDR<0.05. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Actg1 rose log2FC +0.695 (FDR 1.32e-16) and Flna +0.802 (FDR 2.54e-13); in 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut, Actg1 rose +0.651 (FDR 0.00376) and Flna +1.415 (FDR 7.93e-15); in 155 MB Glut, the changes were +0.869 (FDR 3.33e-19) and +0.669 (FDR 0.0212). Direct Actg1 perturbation strongly lowered Actg1 in 151 (-0.824, FDR 9.85e-16) but did not significantly induce Flna there; its only non-self FDR hit was Flna in 027 (+0.779, FDR 0.0132). Actb itself was absent from response rows, and mRNA does not measure actin protein stoichiometry, polymerization, or morphology.
research_community: Actin-autoregulation, neuronal-cytoskeleton, migration, and Baraitser-Winter researchers would find the asymmetry useful. Isotype-specific protein quantification, polymerization imaging, and reciprocal coding-sequence/UTR rescue after defined Actb and Actg1 alleles would distinguish locus regulation from protein demand. Confirmation would support a focused neuronal study of actin-isotype compensation.

finding_title: CAML perturbation lowers receptor, ion-pump, and synaptic-vesicle transcripts
core_idea: Observation: Caml perturbation lowered receptor and membrane genes in thalamic neurons and vesicle, chloride-transporter, ion-pump, and receptor genes in midbrain glutamatergic neurons. Interpretation: loss of the WRB–CAML tail-anchored-protein insertion machinery creates a neuronal membrane-protein liability reflected at the RNA level, although insertion and localization were not measured.
significance: The response extends established ER insertion biology into mature neuronal receptor and vesicle maintenance and supplies concrete readouts for mechanistic work. Its expected contribution is moderate because the pathway itself is known and the transcript changes could be secondary compensation.
prior_expectation: CAML/CAMLG was already part of the mammalian WRB receptor for ER insertion of tail-anchored proteins (Yamamoto and Sakisaka 2012 (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/23041287/); Vilardi et al. 2014 (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24392163/); Reactome WRB–CAMLG docking (https://reactome.org/content/detail/R-HSA-9609899)). A membrane-protein response was plausible, but the neuronal receptor and vesicle transcript set was not directly predicted.
support_and_caveats: In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Caml perturbation lowered Lingo1 (log2FC -0.327, FDR 3.88e-4), Gabrd (-0.281, FDR 0.00239), Gabra1 (-0.286, FDR 0.0134), Syp (-0.207, FDR 0.0154), and Caml (-0.375, FDR 0.0285); 28 genes passed FDR. In 155 MB Glut, it lowered Sv2a (-0.420, FDR 0.00303), Caml (-0.553, FDR 0.00336), Syp (-0.246, FDR 0.00669), Slc12a5 (-0.397, FDR 0.00849), Atp1a3 (-0.227, FDR 0.00857), and Gabbr1 (-0.295, FDR 0.0208); 18 genes passed FDR. Most other contexts had no corrected downstream response, but those nulls do not establish intrinsic restriction. Direct tail-anchor insertion, receptor surface abundance, ER stress, and synaptic function were not assayed.
research_community: Tail-anchored-protein insertion, synaptic-membrane trafficking, and neuronal proteostasis researchers would be the main audience. Surface proteomics and insertion reporters after matched CAML and WRB loss, with CAML rescue, would determine whether the RNA state follows failed insertion of specific neuronal cargos. Confirmation would support a focused program on how ER insertion capacity maintains synaptic membrane composition.

finding_title: SRSF1 perturbation rewires splice-regulator abundance instead of inducing SRSF2 compensation
core_idea: Observation: Srsf1 perturbation increased Ptbp2, Rbm28, Dazap1, and Psip1 while lowering Srsf2, Hnrnpdl, Clk4, and Clk1 in responsive neurons. Interpretation: SRSF1 loss destabilizes a broader RNA-regulator network rather than eliciting simple SRSF2 or CLK-family transcriptional compensation.
significance: The response identifies a concrete abundance-level network reaction to loss of a core SR protein and can guide isoform-focused experiments. It is a moderate-priority extension because direct splicing outcomes and functional compensation remain unknown.
prior_expectation: SRSF1 was already established as an essential SR-family splicing regulator (UniProt SRSF1 (https://rest.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/Q6PDM2)), and interaction/enrichment resources place the response genes in a shared RNA-processing neighborhood (STRING (https://string-db.org/)). The signed collapse of Srsf2 and CLK transcripts rather than compensatory induction was not guaranteed by those priors.
support_and_caveats: In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Srsf1 perturbation strongly lowered Srsf1 (log2FC -1.832, FDR 7.05e-65) and Srsf2 (-1.222, FDR 1.09e-44), while increasing Ptbp2 (+1.194, FDR 2.99e-72), Rbm28 (+1.248, FDR 4.09e-67), Dazap1 (+1.260, FDR 9.95e-65), and Psip1 (+0.999, FDR 4.94e-64). Related, uneven RNA-processing responses occurred in CA3/CA2/DG glutamatergic and hypothalamic or striatal GABAergic contexts. The very broad thalamic response may include secondary stress, and total RNA abundance neither measures splice isoforms nor demonstrates loss of functional SRSF2 compensation.
research_community: Spliceosome, SR-protein, neuronal RNA-processing, and RBP-disease researchers would be most interested. Long-read RNA-seq, phospho-SR proteomics, and SRSF2 or CLK rescue after matched SRSF1 depletion would distinguish failed compensation from downstream network remodeling. Confirmation would support a focused study of SR-network homeostasis in neurons.

finding_title: HSF1 perturbation lowers a basal HSPH1-HSP90 support module
core_idea: Observation: Hsf1 perturbation lowered Hsph1, Hsp90aa1, Hsp90ab1, Ahsa2, Stip1, and Rsrp1 in selected neuronal classes. Interpretation: HSF1 maintains a compact constitutive chaperone support layer in mature neurons, distinct from the sparse response to direct Hsp90ab1 loss.
significance: The result provides cell-resolved evidence for basal, not merely heat-induced, HSF1 control of neuronal chaperone abundance. It is a useful validation and refinement of established feedback biology with moderate follow-up value.
