prior_expectation: HSF1 was already the central heat-shock transcription factor (Reactome HSF1 activation (https://reactome.org/content/detail/R-HSA-3371511); Gomez-Pastor et al. 2018 (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28852220/)), and HSP90 regulation was well characterized (Prodromou 2016 (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4980810/)). Basal maintenance of a compact chaperone module was therefore plausible.
support_and_caveats: In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Hsf1 perturbation lowered Hsph1 (log2FC -0.484, FDR 1.69e-8), Hsp90aa1 (-0.282, FDR 2.85e-4), Rsrp1 (-0.175, FDR 8.06e-4), Hsp90ab1 (-0.345, FDR 8.96e-4), Mat2a (-0.234, FDR 0.00737), and Ahsa2 (-0.294, FDR 0.00827). In 155 MB Glut, Hsph1 fell -0.599 (FDR 2.50e-4), Rsrp1 -0.161 (FDR 0.00169), and Stip1 -0.388 (FDR 0.00583); 052 Pvalb Gaba lowered Rsrp1 and Ahsa2, and 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut lowered Hsp90aa1 -0.439 (FDR 0.0275). Hsf1 self RNA never passed FDR despite predominantly negative trends, which is non-diagnostic for functional editing. Protein abundance, heat-shock inducibility, aggregation, and survival were not measured.
research_community: Heat-shock, neuronal proteostasis, and chaperone-therapy researchers would be the natural audience. Matched HSF1 depletion with chromatin occupancy, basal and induced chaperone proteomics, heat-stress survival, and HSF1 rescue would test direct maintenance of the module. Confirmation would support a focused study of basal HSF1 dependence across neuronal states.

finding_title: CTCF perturbation robustly represses clustered protocadherins in thalamic and midbrain neurons
core_idea: Observation: Ctcf perturbation coordinately lowered multiple α-, β-, and γ-clustered protocadherins in thalamic and midbrain glutamatergic neurons, alongside a recurrent Zcwpw2-up and Dennd6b/Abhd14b-down branch. Interpretation: the atlas recovers established CTCF control of clustered protocadherin loci and adds a cell-resolved mature-neuronal abundance profile.
significance: This is a strong positive control for relational recovery and a useful map of adult neuronal response, but the central CTCF–protocadherin relationship is already established. Follow-up should focus on the less-explained companion branch and cell-state consequences rather than present a new locus mechanism.
prior_expectation: Neuronal CTCF was already required for stochastic clustered-protocadherin expression, dendritic development, and synapse formation (Hirayama et al. 2012 (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22854024/)), and for experience-dependent neuronal gene regulation and chromatin structure (Sams et al. 2016 (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/27880914/)). Coordinated Pcdh-cluster repression was therefore expected.
support_and_caveats: In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Ctcf perturbation lowered Pcdhb20 (log2FC -1.521, FDR 1.47e-7), Pcdhb17 (-1.618, FDR 2.53e-7), Pcdhb16 (-1.910, FDR 2.55e-7), Pcdhac1 (-1.386, FDR 3.28e-7), Pcdhb18 (-1.402, FDR 2.08e-5), and Pcdha10 (-1.106, FDR 1.00e-4). In 155 MB Glut, it lowered Pcdhgb2 (-2.114, FDR 4.17e-5), Pcdhga12 (-1.745, FDR 7.36e-5), Pcdhb20 (-1.933, FDR 7.36e-5), Pcdhb18 (-2.478, FDR 3.51e-5), and Pcdha10 (-1.726, FDR 2.82e-5). The same two classes also showed Zcwpw2 induction and Dennd6b/Abhd14b repression. The assay did not measure CTCF occupancy, chromatin loops, or single-cell protocadherin choice, and the companion genes could reflect a broader state change.
research_community: Chromatin-architecture, protocadherin, and neuronal-identity researchers would use this chiefly as an in vivo perturbation map. CTCF CUT&RUN, locus-conformation assays, and single-cell long-read protocadherin profiling after matched loss would verify whether abundance changes reflect altered promoter choice and looping. The proportionate follow-up is to define the unexplained Zcwpw2/Dennd6b/Abhd14b branch and its relationship to the known locus phenotype.

finding_title: Sec63 perturbation induces an ER-chaperone response distinct from selected secretory-pathway perturbations
core_idea: Sec63 perturbation increased Hspa5, Canx, Hyou1, and Chac1 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, with an Hspa5 echo in 155 MB Glut. Perturbations of Ssr4, Stt3b, Sec23a, Sar1b, Ergic1, and Edem3 showed different expression profiles from this chaperone combination. The pattern defines a SEC63-associated ER import and folding-stress response for comparison with neighboring secretory-pathway perturbations.
significance: The compact response offers a neuronal assay for SEC63 insufficiency and separates it from several neighboring secretory-pathway perturbations at the RNA endpoint. It is a useful mechanistic refinement of established ER-import biology, with limited broader impact until client proteins and functional consequences are identified.
prior_expectation: SEC63 was expected to assist SEC61-mediated ER import based on mammalian transport experiments by Lang and colleagues (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22375059/), and its disease relevance includes impaired polycystin biogenesis in genetic interaction studies (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/21685914/). CHAC1 is a known ATF4-ATF3-CHOP output from UPR studies (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/19109178/), so chaperone and Chac1 induction were consistent with import stress.
support_and_caveats: In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut after Sec63 perturbation, Hspa5 increased by log2FC +0.924 (FDR 6.31e-4), Canx by +0.723 (FDR 0.00607), Hyou1 by +0.633 (FDR 0.00876), and Chac1 by +2.030 (FDR 0.0179). Hspa5 also increased in 155 MB Glut by +1.028 (FDR 0.0298). In 151, Ssr4, Stt3b, and Ergic1 each showed strong FDR-supported self-transcript depletion (-0.640, FDR 5.65e-5; -0.619, FDR 3.69e-4; and -0.820, FDR 2.56e-17, respectively) without the reported Sec63 chaperone module, but equivalent protein-level disruption and client load were not measured. Sec63 itself lacked an FDR self-row in the available evidence.
research_community: ER-translocation and SEC63-disease researchers could determine whether the response reflects failure of a restricted client set. Confirmed SEC63 editing should be followed by translocation reporters with diverse signal peptides, ER proteomics, BiP occupancy, and rescue by wild-type versus J-domain-defective SEC63, alongside matched Ssr4 and Stt3b controls. Identification of the clients whose import failure precedes the chaperone state would support a focused neuronal SEC63 mechanism.

finding_title: ADNP perturbation defines a CHD4-adjacent neuronal signature across thalamic, midbrain, caudal GABAergic, and Pvalb populations
core_idea: ADNP perturbation produced a distributed response comprising 25 FDR genes in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, three in 155 MB Glut, two in 191 MB P MY GABA, and one in 052 Pvalb Gaba, with recurrent Cacnb3 induction and Plppr3 or Atp9a repression. A report-level signature comparison placed CHD4 nearest to ADNP in 151 and 155. This marker pattern defines a mature-neuronal ADNP output aligned with the established ADNP–CHD4 ChAHP relationship.
significance: If reproduced, the result would provide a compact set of neuronal readouts for testing an established ADNP–CHD4 complex in postnatal neurons. Its value is mainly to extend known ChAHP biology into several mature neuronal populations and to identify tractable markers, consistent with moderate rather than program-defining priority.
prior_expectation: Human genetics established ADNP as an autism and intellectual-disability gene (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24531329/), and biochemical work placed ADNP and CHD4 together in the ChAHP complex (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29795351/). Some convergence was therefore expected; the sparse, marker-level neuronal output is the atlas-specific extension.
support_and_caveats: After Adnp perturbation, Xylt2 decreased by log2FC -0.925 (FDR 1.54e-10), Cpne7 decreased by -0.906 (FDR 1.81e-9), and Vstm2l increased by +1.583 (FDR 7.76e-6) in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut. Cacnb3 increased in 052 Pvalb Gaba (+1.093, FDR 2.70e-5) and 155 MB Glut (+0.863, FDR 1.23e-4), while Plppr3 decreased in 191 MB P MY GABA (-1.054, FDR 0.0335). The CHD4 link comes from signature proximity rather than chromatin occupancy, and the small, nonidentical marker sets leave generic perturbation-state or indirect transcriptional effects as alternatives.
research_community: ADNP syndrome, ChAHP, and neuronal chromatin communities could use these markers to ask whether an established complex has a distinct postnatal role. A decisive test would combine independently validated ADNP editing with CHD4 occupancy or CUT&Tag at the implicated loci and ADNP rescue in the same neuronal populations. Confirmation would justify a focused study of mature-neuron ChAHP targets, not yet a broad new program.

finding_title: PPP2R1A perturbation defines a cortical Amy1-high, Rsrp1/Leng8-low reporter state with TSC/STXBP1 neighborhood structure
core_idea: In 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, PPP2R1A perturbation induced Amy1, Rnpc3, Stmn4, Jun, Pcsk1n, Ovgp1, and related transcripts while repressing Rsrp1, Leng8, Kifc2, and Pabpn1. Signature comparisons placed this cortical marker panel near TSC/STXBP1-positive and LIMK1/DNAJB6-negative states. The resulting reporter profile provides an atlas-defined phenotype for testing how PP2A scaffold perturbation relates to these cortical signaling contexts.
significance: The panel could become a useful RNA phenotype for testing how PP2A scaffold disruption affects mature cortical neurons, including neurodevelopmental-disease alleles. At present it is more likely to support a bounded follow-up study than change PP2A pathway models.
prior_expectation: PP2A is organized from scaffold, catalytic, and regulatory subunits (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/17174897/), and PPP2R1A or PPP2R5D variants cause PP2A-related intellectual disability (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26168268/). A neuronal transcriptional consequence was plausible, but this exact Amy1/RNA-processing marker combination was not an established expectation.
support_and_caveats: PPP2R1A perturbation in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut increased Amy1 by log2FC +1.181 (FDR 3.02e-18), Rnpc3 by +0.676 (FDR 2.70e-14), and Stmn4 by +0.475 (FDR 8.33e-7), while decreasing Rsrp1 by -0.379 (FDR 1.16e-11), Leng8 by -0.359 (FDR 3.53e-9), and Kifc2 by -0.379 (FDR 3.35e-8). These rows firmly support a reporter state, but the neighbor correlations were report-derived and no phosphatase activity, PP2A holoenzyme composition, or TSC/STXBP1 epistasis was measured.
research_community: PP2A neurodevelopmental-disease and cortical signaling researchers would be the most direct audience. Isogenic PPP2R1A editing followed by phosphatase-complex profiling and rescue with wild-type versus disease alleles would distinguish a PP2A-dependent state from guide or stress effects; targeted TSC1/STXBP1 epistasis could then test the tentative neighborhood. A positive result would yield a practical assay for allele stratification.

finding_title: Distinct endomembrane perturbations converge on a proteostasis-associated neighborhood with node-specific outputs
core_idea: The atlas places ATP6V0C, CAML, PI4KA, DHDDS, VPS53, and VPS54 perturbations near endomembrane or proteostasis states, with node-specific leading outputs: ATP6V0C lowers Atp6v0a1, CAML raises Stmn4, and PI4KA lowers Slc12a5. These results define a many-to-one neighborhood in which acidification, membrane insertion, phosphoinositide synthesis, glycosylation, and tethering converge on related RNA states. The shared neighborhood and its node-specific outputs provide a framework for separating common organelle responses from pathway-specific effects.
significance: This view could help endomembrane researchers select shared stress readouts while preserving the distinct initiating lesions. Because the group is heterogeneous and supported partly by modest correlations, it currently refines experimental organization more than it establishes a new pathway.
prior_expectation: ATP6V0C is a V-ATPase V0 pore component (https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P63082), PI4KA maintains plasma-membrane PI4P and PI(4,5)P2 pools (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24415756/), DHDDS supplies dolichyl-phosphate for glycosylation (https://reactome.org/content/detail/R-HSA-4419978), and VPS53 participates in endocytic recycling (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25799061/). Convergence at a broad endomembrane-stress level was therefore plausible, whereas a single shared neuronal mechanism was not.
support_and_caveats: ATP6V0C perturbation reduced Atp6v0a1 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut (log2FC -0.577, FDR 2.39e-19), 155 MB Glut (-0.438, FDR 6.82e-13), and 052 Pvalb Gaba (-0.450, FDR 1.29e-7). CAML perturbation increased Stmn4 in 191 MB P MY GABA (+1.068, FDR 1.83e-4) and 052 Pvalb Gaba (+0.833, FDR 0.00363); PI4KA perturbation reduced Slc12a5 in 191 MB P MY GABA (-0.670, FDR 0.0136). The broader neighborhood rests on correlation and low-count marker findings, and the PI4KA pineal branch is low-n; shared RNA proximity cannot establish common flux, organelle physiology, or causal ordering.
research_community: Neuronal membrane-trafficking, lysosome, and proteostasis groups could test whether the shared neighborhood reflects a common organelle state. Parallel perturbations with live endolysosomal pH, PI4P, glycosylation, and cargo-trafficking measurements would determine whether the RNA overlap tracks one physiological variable or several. The proportionate outcome would be a cross-node phenotyping framework and a small number of mechanistically coherent subgroups.

finding_title: KLF9 perturbation defines a Wsb1/Rasgrp2/Pld3 thalamic module distinct from KLF7 and KLF13 outputs
core_idea: Klf9-assigned cells in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut showed 19 FDR genes, including increased Wsb1, Rasgrp2, Pld3, Dzip1, Maged2, Hcn3, and Aplp1. Klf7 and Klf13 perturbations showed different leading marker directions in the same context. Together, these results define a KLF9-associated mature-thalamic state that distinguishes this perturbation from the selected KLF paralogs.
significance: The result could identify a few downstream markers for comparing hormone-responsive KLF paralogs in mature neurons. Its mechanism and consequence are presently too narrow for more than a low-priority validation study.
prior_expectation: Klf9 is directly induced by thyroid hormone in the postnatal brain (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/19359381/) and is required for late neuronal maturation (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/19657039/). KLF paralogs can differ in their effects on CNS axon growth (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/19815778/), so paralog non-equivalence was plausible even though this marker set was unexpected.
support_and_caveats: Under Klf9 guides in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Wsb1 rose by log2FC +0.316 (FDR 1.31e-7), Rasgrp2 by +0.759 (FDR 2.16e-6), Pld3 by +0.560 (FDR 5.60e-6), Dzip1 by +0.414 (FDR 1.34e-5), Hcn3 by +0.921 (FDR 3.88e-4), and Aplp1 by +0.291 (FDR 0.00533). Klf9 itself changed by -0.138 with FDR 1.0. In Klf7 and Klf13 perturbations, Wsb1, Rasgrp2, and Pld3 were not FDR-supported; however, unequal functional editing could still explain the apparent paralog boundary, and the weak SIN3A similarity does not establish a corepressor mechanism.
research_community: Thyroid-hormone, stress-hormone, and neuronal KLF researchers could validate the marker set with independent Klf9 guides, protein-level disruption, and rescue. KLF9 occupancy at Wsb1, Rasgrp2, and Pld3 would distinguish direct regulation from a secondary state. If confirmed, this would support a focused mature-neuron KLF9 regulon study.

finding_title: ZMYM2 perturbation induces a Notum/Echdc2/F11r/Atp2a3 thalamic signature
core_idea: Zmym2 guides yielded 22 FDR genes in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, with strong induction of Echdc2, F11r, Atp2a3, Ebf4, and Notum. This marker state links ZMYM2 perturbation to Notum signaling and Atp2a3-associated calcium handling in mature thalamic neurons. The implicated genes provide defined targets for testing ZMYM2-dependent chromatin regulation.
significance: The signature offers a small set of candidate readouts for studying ZMYM2 in mature neurons and testing whether Notum or calcium handling is affected. Without recurrence, occupancy, or functional consequence, it remains an incremental, low-priority extension of ZMYM2 chromatin biology.
prior_expectation: ZMYM2 participates in chromatin corepressor complexes (https://elifesciences.org/articles/86669), and heterozygous loss-of-function variants cause a syndromic congenital disorder (https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ajhg.2020.08.013). Those priors predicted transcriptional effects, but not this specific Notum/Atp2a3 combination.
support_and_caveats: In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Zmym2 perturbation increased Echdc2 by log2FC +1.343 (FDR 1.30e-11), F11r by +1.069 (FDR 4.31e-10), Atp2a3 by +2.262 (FDR 7.15e-10), Ebf4 by +1.346 (FDR 3.58e-8), and Notum by +0.933 (FDR 4.10e-5). The measured Zmym2 transcript was not FDR-reduced in any class, and no supplied evidence connects ZMYM2 directly to these genes; guide-specific effects or an indirect state change remain substantial alternatives.
research_community: ZMYM2 syndrome and chromatin-corepressor groups could perform independent editing and wild-type rescue in the same neuronal class, followed by ZMYM2 occupancy and calcium-store assays centered on Atp2a3. Confirmation would justify a narrow study of this mature-neuronal output rather than a broad disease program.

finding_title: SP4 perturbation defines a Tsga10/Abhd11/Svip module in posterior glutamatergic neurons
core_idea: The atlas reports corrected responses for SP4 perturbation in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, with Tsga10 and Abhd11 induction and supporting Svip, Strada, and Dnajc4 changes. This posterior glutamatergic marker program is distinct from developmental SP4–NMDAR biology. It provides an adult-neuron context for testing SP4 regulation of Tsga10, Abhd11, and the associated genes.
significance: Tsga10 and Abhd11 could be useful readouts for testing an adult SP4 state, but the current evidence does not assign a function to the module. The necessary first step is data-label and perturbation validation, making this a low-priority lead.
prior_expectation: Curated annotation describes SP4 as a nuclear GC/GT-box-binding transcription factor (https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/Q02446/entry), while brain-expression resources show broad rather than sharply regional SP4 expression (https://www.proteinatlas.org/ENSG00000105866-SP4). A posterior Tsga10/Abhd11 state was not an established expectation.
support_and_caveats: The detailed rows label the corrected marker set as 155 MB Glut: Svip log2FC +0.643 (FDR 3.17e-6), Strada +0.469 (FDR 2.23e-5), Tsga10 +0.772 (FDR 7.23e-4), Dnajc4 +0.608 (FDR 0.0146), and Abhd11 +0.529 (FDR 0.0298). A separate evidence summary assigns a strong signature to 151 and a second signature to 155, but its quoted values do not match those detailed cell labels. That inconsistency, together with increased rather than decreased Sp4 RNA, prevents a stronger biological conclusion.
research_community: SP-family and adult neuronal transcription researchers should first reproduce the contrast from the source matrix and verify cell labels, then use independent SP4 editing, protein measurement, and rescue. SP4 occupancy at Tsga10 and Abhd11 would distinguish direct transcriptional control from a guide-associated state. Until then, only a small validation project is warranted.

finding_title: ZFP148 perturbation lowers spliceosomal and synaptic-marker transcripts in thalamic Prkcd/Grin2c neurons
core_idea: Zfp148 perturbation produced its corrected response in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, where Srrm2, Srsf9, Cacnb3, Slitrk5, Ptprn, and Rasgrp2 decreased. The resulting marker state connects ZFP148 perturbation with spliceosome-associated and synaptic transcripts. Comparisons with TRP53, HDAC8, CELF2, and ESRRA position it as a distinct atlas-defined state for testing transcriptional and splicing consequences.
significance: The finding provides a testable entry point into an understudied neuronal output of ZNF148. Because the program is small and no altered isoforms or direct targets were measured, its likely near-term value is a focused mechanistic note rather than a broad research direction.
prior_expectation: Reactome places SRSF9, SRRM2, and LUC7L2 in mRNA-splicing machinery (https://reactome.org/content/detail/R-HSA-72163), while ZNF148 paralog cooperation is known to be context dependent (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37948511/). These priors make the marker identities interpretable but do not predict direct ZFP148 control of them.
support_and_caveats: Within 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Zfp148 perturbation decreased Srrm2 by log2FC -0.288 (FDR 0.00164), Cacnb3 by -0.939 (FDR 0.00255), Srsf9 by -0.569 (FDR 0.0103), Slitrk5 by -0.762 (FDR 0.0295), and Ptprn and Rasgrp2 by -0.350 and -0.948 (both FDR 0.0450). Luc7l2 was just outside threshold (-0.249, FDR 0.0543), and Zfp148 itself was unchanged (-0.044, FDR 1.0). The major gap is that abundance changes in splice factors do not demonstrate altered splicing or direct ZFP148 regulation.
research_community: Neuronal transcription and RNA-splicing groups could test independently edited Zfp148 neurons by long-read or junction-level RNA sequencing, coupled to ZFP148 occupancy and rescue. A reproducible isoform consequence would turn the marker panel into a defined ZFP148–splicing study; without it, the result should remain a small observational lead.

finding_title: NR2F1 perturbation couples Sorl1 induction to Sema7a repression in thalamic Prkcd/Grin2c neurons
core_idea: Nr2f1 perturbation increased Sorl1 and decreased Sema7a at FDR significance in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut. Cortical L5-6 IT and CTX-CGE GABA populations exhibited different downstream profiles. Together, the results define an adult NR2F1-associated thalamic response centered on opposing membrane-trafficking and guidance genes.
significance: The opposing Sorl1/Sema7a pair is easy to retest and may connect an established developmental transcription factor to mature neuronal membrane or guidance biology. Two genes and one responsive population limit its expected impact to a low-priority follow-up.
prior_expectation: NR2F1 is an established neurodevelopmental transcription factor associated with Bosch-Boonstra-Schaaf optic atrophy syndrome (https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK587319/), and earlier work established important neural functions for COUP-TF family dosage (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/18165280/). A sparse adult Sorl1/Sema7a response was not the obvious prediction.
support_and_caveats: In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Nr2f1 perturbation increased Sorl1 by log2FC +0.488 (FDR 0.00994) and decreased Sema7a by -0.350 (FDR 0.0407). Nr2f1 itself was only nominally lower (-0.225, FDR 1.0); Chst1, Igsf21, Lrrtm4, Ncan, and Plxdc1 were also nominal rather than FDR-supported. The two-gene output may be indirect, and silence in other populations is not evidence of thalamic specificity under unequal power.
research_community: NR2F1 neurodevelopment and adult projection-neuron researchers could retest the pair with independent guides, DNA/protein editing assays, and NR2F1 rescue. Occupancy at Sorl1 and Sema7a, followed by neurite or synaptic phenotyping, would decide whether this is direct regulation with a functional consequence. Confirmation would motivate a compact adult-NR2F1 study.

finding_title: KLF7 perturbation links Tuba1a repression to a thalamic cytoskeletal transcript pattern
core_idea: In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Klf7 perturbation decreased Tuba1a, accompanied by directionally aligned changes in Coro1a, Sptan1, Stmn2, Map1b, Map6, and Dctn1. This pattern defines a cytoskeletal readout for studying KLF7-dependent projection maintenance in mature thalamic neurons. It also connects the adult perturbation response to KLF7's established developmental role in neuronal morphogenesis.
significance: The result can nominate Tuba1a as a sensitive marker for testing KLF7 function in mature neurons. Its sparse support and lack of the expected Ntrk1/CDKN/Rac3 outputs make it incremental and low priority.
prior_expectation: KLF7 is expressed during neurogenesis (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/11336497/) and mouse genetics established roles in neuronal morphogenesis (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15964824/). Those studies predicted axonal or cytoskeletal consequences, so the broad direction is not surprising even though the adult thalamic marker is new.
support_and_caveats: For Klf7-assigned nuclei from 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Tuba1a decreased by log2FC -0.281 (FDR 0.0123). Coro1a (-0.432, FDR 0.0526), Sptan1 (-0.135, FDR 0.0902), Stmn2 (-0.248, FDR 0.180), Map1b (-0.193, FDR 0.464), Map6 (-0.220, FDR 0.690), and Dctn1 (-0.139, FDR 0.748) did not clear 5% FDR. Klf7 RNA itself was unchanged (-0.059, FDR 1.0), and Ntrk1, Cdkn1a, Cdkn1b, and Rac3 were unsupported; the apparent module could therefore reflect a single robust marker plus correlated nominal noise.
research_community: Axon-growth and KLF researchers could validate Tuba1a with independent Klf7 editing, KLF7 protein loss, and rescue, then test microtubule organization or axonal transport. Only if the weaker cytoskeletal genes and a cellular phenotype replicate would a larger mature-neuron KLF7 project be justified.

finding_title: Dctn1 loss selectively activates a neuronal sterol-biosynthesis program
core_idea: The dynactin subunit perturbation Dctn1 upregulated SREBP/cholesterol genes rather than producing only a generic transport signature. The program was strongest in midbrain glutamatergic and pons/medulla GABA neurons and recurred across 12 neuronal classes, suggesting that dynein-dynactin disruption rapidly couples retrograde transport stress to lipid-homeostatic transcription in postmitotic neurons. This is a biological interpretation; the direct observation is concerted induction of Insig1, Msmo1, Hmgcs1, Fdps, Ldlr, Hmgcr, Nsdhl, Fdft1, Sc5d, and Sqle after Dctn1 perturbation.
significance: DCTN1 is a causal gene for Perry syndrome and related ALS/frontotemporal/parkinsonian phenotypes, but the atlas points to sterol synthesis as an early neuronal response to partial loss of dynactin. If validated, this gives transport-neurodegeneration groups a concrete lipid axis to perturb genetically and pharmacologically before overt aggregate pathology appears.
prior_expectation: DCTN1 was expected to affect axonal transport, stress granule dynamics, and TDP-43 pathology; DCTN1 disease reviews emphasize dynactin transport failure in Perry syndrome and motor-neuron disease (Konno et al., 2017, PMID: 28625595), and DCTN1 deficiency can exacerbate TDP-43 aggregation by impairing stress-granule resolution (Ueda et al., 2024, PMID: 38311779). A synchronized cholesterol-biosynthesis response in acute juvenile brain neurons was not the obvious expected output.
support_and_caveats: Dctn1 had 358 changed genes across 12 cell classes at FDR < 0.05 and |log2FC| >= 0.25. In 155 MB Glut, canonical sterol genes were among the top hits: Insig1 log2FC +2.07, q = 4.42e-55; Msmo1 +1.90, q = 1.38e-44; Hmgcs1 +1.61, q = 1.48e-41; Fdps +2.14, q = 3.29e-40; Ldlr +2.23, q = 1.34e-35; Hmgcr +1.48, q = 6.50e-34. The same module appeared in 191 MB P MY GABA, including Insig1 +1.80, q = 1.95e-27; Fdps +2.26, q = 6.82e-24; Msmo1 +1.86, q = 1.29e-22; and Dhcr24 +1.62, q = 1.65e-21. The result is transcriptionally coherent, but it is still a sparse-CRISPR RNA readout: the sterol increase may be compensatory, may reflect altered lysosomal cholesterol sensing, or may be a survivor bias among damaged cells.
research_community: ALS/FTD, Perry syndrome, axonal-transport, lipid-metabolism, and lysosome investigators would be the natural audience. The strongest follow-up program would combine acute Dctn1 knockout in defined midbrain neurons with SREBP reporter imaging, filipin or mass-spectrometry sterol measurements, dynein/dynactin rescue constructs, and tests of whether SREBP or cholesterol-synthesis inhibition modifies TDP-43 or alpha-synuclein stress.

finding_title: Wdr26 loss produces a cerebellar GABA channel-and-splicing signature
core_idea: Wdr26 perturbation caused the largest cerebellar signature in the atlas, with 1,444 changed genes in 308 CB GABA. The observation is simultaneous loss of RNA-splicing and ion-channel transcripts such as Srrm2, Luc7l2, Kpna1, Cacna1g, Kalrn, Grik1, and Dagla, together with induction of Serpini1 and Kcnt1. The biological interpretation is that WDR26-containing CTLH/GID ubiquitin-ligase assemblies maintain postnatal cerebellar inhibitory-neuron excitability and RNA-processing state.
significance: WDR26 haploinsufficiency causes Skraban-Deardorff neurodevelopmental syndrome, but the immediate vulnerable neuronal program has been unclear. This atlas suggests an adult-maintenance role in cerebellar GABA neurons, which shifts the disease model from general developmental delay toward a testable failure of channel and splicing homeostasis in inhibitory cerebellar circuits.
prior_expectation: Recent structural work showed that Skraban-Deardorff mutations in WDR26 impair CTLH E3 ligase assembly and substrate-receptor functions (Gross et al., 2024, PMID: 38575527). That precedent predicted disrupted ubiquitin-ligase biology, not the specific Cacna1g/Grik1/Srrm2 program in cerebellar GABA neurons.
support_and_caveats: The Wdr26 signature was concentrated but large: 1,444 genes in 308 CB GABA, 470 in 155 MB Glut, and 324 in 191 MB P MY GABA. In 308 CB GABA, top effects included Srrm2 -0.799, q = 1.95e-11; Kalrn -1.28, q = 6.51e-10; Luc7l2 -0.716, q = 6.51e-10; Cacna1g -1.74, q = 6.51e-10; Kpna1 -0.784, q = 6.51e-10; Grik1 -1.46, q = 8.30e-09; and Kcnt1 +1.58, q = 7.48e-09. Srrm2 was also down in 155 MB Glut (-0.693, q = 7.09e-19) and 191 MB P MY GABA (-0.835, q = 4.68e-12). The caveat is that only five classes passed the signature threshold, so the cerebellar enrichment could reflect WDR26 biology, cerebellar sensitivity to CRISPR mosaicism, or both.
research_community: Skraban-Deardorff syndrome groups, cerebellar ataxia investigators, CTLH/GID complex biochemists, and channelopathy researchers would all have reason to pursue this. Promising grants would pair Wdr26 conditional deletion in cerebellar interneuron subclasses with patch-clamp tests of T-type calcium and BK sodium-activated potassium currents, rescue by wild-type versus syndrome WDR26 alleles, and proteomic identification of CTLH substrates controlling Srrm2 or channel expression.

finding_title: Acute Tsc1 and Tsc2 loss couples mTOR derepression to a sterol-lysosome module in postnatal neurons
core_idea: Tsc1 and the lower-coverage Tsc2 perturbations converged on induction of lysosomal and cholesterol-associated transcripts, including Atp6v0b, Lamp2, Dpp7, Mcoln1, Cpeb1, Insig1, Cyp51, Msmo1, Ldlr, and Pik3r3. The observation appeared most strongly in 155 MB Glut and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut. The interpretation is that partial mosaic loss of the TSC complex is enough to engage an mTORC1-linked lysosomal/SREBP response in mature excitatory and inhibitory neurons.
significance: TSC biology is central to epilepsy and autism, but this juvenile whole-brain Perturb-seq view tests the response outside embryonic cortical germline models. The data prioritize lipid/lysosome transcripts as rapid neuronal effectors to follow alongside cell-size and excitability phenotypes.
prior_expectation: TSC1/TSC2 are established negative regulators of mTORC1; Tsc1 deletion reactivates mTOR and can promote adult CNS axon regeneration (Park et al., 2008, PMID: 18988856), and focal cortical models show that Tsc1, Pten, Depdc5, Rheb, and Mtor mutations have both convergent and gene-specific effects on cortical neurons (Nguyen et al., 2024, PMID: 38411613). A cholesterol/lysosome readout was plausible but not the canonical first phenotype.
support_and_caveats: Tsc1 produced 1,062 changed genes in 15 cell classes; Tsc2 produced 384 in 8. In 155 MB Glut, Tsc1 raised Cpeb1 +1.16, q = 2.44e-28; Atp6v0b +0.526, q = 1.40e-21; Pik3r3 +1.36, q = 2.26e-17; Lamp2 +0.782, q = 3.16e-12; and Insig1 +1.02, q = 2.22e-10. Tsc2 in the same cell class raised overlapping sterol and lysosome genes: Cyp51 +0.730, q = 6.42e-09; Cpeb1 +0.698, q = 1.39e-08; Insig1 +0.908, q = 7.05e-08; Atp6v0b +0.305, q = 9.52e-08; Msmo1 +0.873, q = 1.06e-07; and Ldlr +1.26, q = 3.05e-07. The interpretation is strengthened by pathway convergence but limited by transcript-only mTOR inference; phospho-S6, TFEB localization, and sterol abundance were not measured.
research_community: Tuberous sclerosis, mTORopathy, epilepsy, cortical malformation, and neuronal lipid biology groups would be highly motivated. A high-value program would perturb Tsc1 or Tsc2 in defined adult neuronal populations, jointly assay phospho-S6, SREBP2 processing, TFEB/TFE3 localization, lysosomal pH, and electrophysiology, then test whether lipid or lysosome modulators alter hyperexcitability independently of rapalogs.

finding_title: Srsf1 loss elicits a pan-neuronal splice-factor autoregulatory response
core_idea: Srsf1 perturbation changed 8,969 genes and was active in all 23 cell classes. The direct observation is that Srsf1 mRNA and other splicing-associated transcripts such as Arglu1, Srsf2, Hnrnpdl, Dazap1, Rbm28, Gpatch8, Psip1, and Xpot were among the most recurrent responses. The interpretation is that postmitotic neurons rely on a tightly buffered SR-protein network, so weakening SRSF1 causes a broad compensatory and mis-splicing transcriptional state rather than a cell-type-limited phenotype.
significance: This is the most pervasive RNA-processing signature in the atlas. It identifies SRSF1 as a central point of fragility in juvenile neurons and gives RNA-splicing researchers a cross-cell-type perturbational baseline for comparing disease RBPs such as TDP-43, MATR3, and CELF2.
prior_expectation: SRSF1 is a core SR-family splicing regulator that negatively autoregulates its own productive splicing and buffers splicing-factor dosage (Ding et al., 2022, PMID: 35732114). Acute SRSF1 depletion can damage tissue homeostasis and produce broad transcriptional and proteomic consequences, including R-loop-associated stress in liver (Arif et al., 2023, PMID: 36759613). Broad effects were expected, but their uniformity across postnatal neuronal classes was not established.
support_and_caveats: At FDR < 0.05 and |log2FC| >= 0.25, Srsf1 had 2,390 changed genes in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 1,342 in 155 MB Glut, 1,092 in 191 MB P MY GABA, 826 in 217 P MY Pineal Glut, 720 in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, and smaller signatures in every remaining class. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, the strongest hits were Fam193b -1.48, q = 1.11e-80; Gpatch8 +1.02, q = 2.94e-73; Ptbp2 +1.19, q = 2.99e-72; Rbm28 +1.25, q = 4.09e-67; Arglu1 -1.04, q = 5.27e-65; and Srsf1 -1.83, q = 7.05e-65. Same-direction recurrence was high: Srsf1 and Arglu1 were down in 22 classes, Psip1 and Far1 were up in 21, and Fam193b, Trim17, and Rbm28 recurred in 20. The caveat is that DE of RNA regulators cannot reveal the causative isoform changes.
research_community: RNA-splicing groups, neuronal RBP labs, and teams building splice-modulating antisense or small-molecule therapies would be most interested. The next experiments are long-read isoform sequencing after Srsf1 deletion, rescue with splicing-active and inactive SRSF1, single-molecule RNA FISH for self-regulatory isoforms, and cell-class comparisons of the same perturbation in organoids and adult mouse brain.

finding_title: Uba5 loss links neuronal UFMylation to mitochondrial translation and V-ATPase repression
core_idea: Perturbing the UFM1 E1 enzyme Uba5 changed 2,942 genes, concentrated in thalamic and midbrain/hindbrain neurons. The direct observation is induction of mitochondrial translation and oxidative-phosphorylation-associated RNAs such as Eef1a1, Ndufa2, Atp5j2, and Uqcc2, together with recurrent repression of Atp6v0c, Syt11, Srsf5, and Rsrp1. The interpretation is that loss of protein UFMylation forces neurons into an ER-mitochondrial compensation state coupled to reduced lysosomal acidification machinery.
significance: UBA5 loss causes developmental and epileptic encephalopathy, but the postmitotic neuronal effector program is not well mapped. The atlas points to a discrete mitochondrial/V-ATPase module that can be followed by UFM1 conjugation proteomics and lysosome assays.
prior_expectation: UFMylation downstream of UBA5 is known to be essential for development and ER stress resistance, and DEE44 variants in UBA5 reduce UFM1 activation to degrees that correlate with in vivo phenotypes in fly and biochemical assays (Pan et al., 2023, PMID: 38079206). The exact neuronal combination of mitochondrial induction plus Atp6v0c repression was not a standard prediction.
support_and_caveats: Uba5 had 2,177 changed genes in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 587 in 155 MB Glut. In thalamic neurons, strong effects included Eef1a1 +0.759, q = 4.76e-26; H1f4 +1.73, q = 4.76e-26; Rsrp1 -0.437, q = 7.65e-26; Abcc5 -0.500, q = 3.52e-25; Trim8 +1.05, q = 1.05e-23; and Ina +0.763, q = 4.00e-22. In 155 MB Glut, Atp6v0c was the top hit at -0.714, q = 1.11e-18, followed by Syt11 -0.580, q = 8.52e-18, Ndufa2 +0.945, q = 2.09e-11, Atp5j2 +0.806, q = 6.89e-10, and Uqcc2 +0.872, q = 1.68e-09. The UFMylation interpretation is coherent but still indirect because the atlas lacks UFM1-modified substrate measurements.
research_community: DEE44/epileptic encephalopathy groups, UFMylation biochemists, ER quality-control investigators, and mitochondrial neurologists are likely audiences. A strong research program would identify UFMylated ribosome-translocon substrates in neurons, then test whether lysosomal acidification or mitochondrial translation modifiers rescue firing and survival after Uba5 loss.

finding_title: Thap11 perturbation reveals a conserved Rabac1-Sdccag8-Gdap1 mitochondrial/ciliary module
core_idea: Thap11 loss produced a distinctive signature in midbrain glutamatergic, thalamic glutamatergic, and subcortical GABA neurons. The same small gene set, including Rabac1, Sdccag8, Gdap1, Mdh1, Ndufa3, Acp6, Trub1, and Slc38a7, fell strongly, whereas Ttc41, Prkn, and Thoc6 rose. The biological interpretation is that THAP11 sustains a cilia/mitochondria/lysosome-adjacent maintenance module in mature neurons.
significance: THAP11 is not as heavily studied in brain as CHD8, SETD1A, or KMT2D, so this repeated compact module is one of the more novel atlas signals. It nominates a tractable regulon connecting Sdccag8 ciliopathy biology, Gdap1 mitochondrial dynamics, and parkin-linked quality control.
prior_expectation: Human neurodevelopmental disorders often converge on chromatin and autophagy regulation, and NDD-linked chromatin factors can regulate autophagy genes in non-neuronal contexts (Lewerissa et al., 2023, PMID:37674294). THAP11 itself had little direct precedent as an acute postmitotic neuronal regulator.
support_and_caveats: Thap11 perturbation changed 184 genes in 155 MB Glut with 327 perturbed nuclei, 373 genes in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut with 297 perturbed nuclei, 162 genes in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA with 171 nuclei, and 125 genes in 191 MB P MY GABA with 136 nuclei. In 155 MB Glut, examples were Rabac1 -1.69, FDR 2.39e-62; Sdccag8 -1.90, FDR 7.82e-49; Gdap1 -1.96, FDR 2.07e-46; Ndufa3 -1.58, FDR 4.22e-42; Acp6 -2.13, FDR 5.42e-33; Ttc41 +3.98, FDR 2.16e-27; and Prkn +0.93, FDR 3.70e-27. The small repeated module is strong, but the target is a transcription factor and the evidence does not distinguish direct THAP11 binding from an indirect ciliary stress state.
research_community: Ciliopathy, mitochondrial-dynamics, and neuronal transcription-factor groups are the best fits. A high-value program would map THAP11 binding near Rabac1, Sdccag8, and Gdap1, image primary cilia and mitophagy in perturbed thalamic and midbrain neurons, and ask whether parkin induction is adaptive or a biomarker of mitochondrial injury.

finding_title: NatB catalytic-subunit loss represses a Peg3-Kifc2-Snhg11 program in many neurons
core_idea: Naa20, the catalytic subunit of the NatB N-terminal acetyltransferase, produced 1,864 changed genes across 15 cell classes. The repeated observation is loss of Snhg11, Kifc2, Peg3, Repin1, Atp11b, Srsf5, Maged1, Cyp46a1, and Tafazzin, strongest in thalamic and midbrain neurons. The interpretation is that NatB-dependent co-translational acetylation stabilizes a neuronal RNA and membrane-trafficking maintenance program.
significance: NatB acetylates a large fraction of proteins, and human NAA20 missense variants cause developmental delay and microcephaly, but neuron-resolved downstream genes are not known. This atlas identifies candidate NatB-sensitive RNAs that can be turned into substrate and rescue studies.
prior_expectation: NAA20 and NAA25 form the NatB complex, whose N-terminal acetyltransferase activity requires complex assembly (Lasa et al., 2020, PMID: 32976911). Recessive NAA20 variants impair NatB formation/activity and cause developmental delay, intellectual disability, and microcephaly (Morrison et al., 2021, PMID: 34230638). The exact Peg3/Kifc2 neuronal module had no direct precedent.
support_and_caveats: The largest Naa20 signature was in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, with 1,132 changed genes; recurrent same-direction hits included Snhg11 down in 9 classes, and Kifc2, Repin1, and Atp11b down in 8 each. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, top responses included Snhg11 -0.367, q = 1.14e-35; Peg3 -0.585, q = 2.53e-30; Gprasp1 -0.763, q = 1.54e-25; Aplp2 -0.573, q = 2.06e-25; Leng8 -0.475, q = 8.20e-25; Kifc2 -0.537, q = 3.20e-24; and Tafazzin -1.13, q = 7.59e-23. The core limitation is that none of these RNAs prove which NatB substrate is causative.
research_community: N-terminal acetylation, protein homeostasis, rare neurodevelopmental disease, and neuronal trafficking groups would be the main audience. Follow-up should combine N-terminomics after Naa20 CRISPR, substrate-specific acetylation rescue, and tests of whether KIFC2, TAFAZZIN, or cholesterol-turnover pathways mediate the transcriptional state.

finding_title: Tpr loss induces a nuclear-transport transcriptional program centered on Ranbp6 and Xpo1
core_idea: The nuclear-pore basket gene Tpr produced 5,087 changed genes across 10 neuronal classes. The direct observation is induction of nuclear-transport and transcriptional regulators such as Ranbp6, Xpo1, Pigm, Tob1, Zfp770, Zfp281, Mga, and Med13, with repeated repression of Leng8, Amy1, Ogt, Rnpc3, and Wsb1. The interpretation is that partial nuclear-pore disruption is sensed as an RNA-export or nucleocytoplasmic-transport stress in postnatal neurons.
significance: Nucleocytoplasmic transport has become a major theme in ALS and other neurodegenerative diseases. This atlas highlights TPR as a high-leverage perturbation in mammalian neurons and nominates compensatory transport factors, especially Ranbp6 and Xpo1, as measurable effectors.
prior_expectation: Nuclear pore components and nucleocytoplasmic shuttling can modify TDP-43 localization and neurotoxicity in RNAi screens and neurons (Kim et al., 2012, PMID: 22872699). A direct juvenile-brain TPR perturbation signature, however, was not known.
support_and_caveats: Tpr changed 2,549 genes in 155 MB Glut, 1,672 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 297 in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, and 246 in 191 MB P MY GABA. In 155 MB Glut, Tob1 was +1.67, q = 1.55e-19; Chd9 +1.23, q = 5.23e-19; Ranbp6 +1.55, q = 3.27e-18; Leng8 -0.854, q = 1.35e-17; Amy1 -1.57, q = 9.71e-17; and Pigm +1.74, q = 5.76e-16. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Xpo1 was +0.955, q = 3.20e-14 while Ogt was -0.626, q = 3.10e-13. The downstream labels fit transport stress, but the atlas does not measure RNA export or protein localization.
research_community: Nuclear-pore, RAN transport, ALS/FTD, repeat-expansion disease, and neuronal RNA-localization researchers would pursue this. Key experiments are single-molecule RNA export assays after Tpr loss, RAN gradient imaging, rescue with TPR basket-domain mutants, and genetic suppression screens for Ranbp6 or Xpo1.

finding_title: Apc loss activates canonical Wnt feedback in Prkcd/Grin2c thalamic neurons
core_idea: Perturbing the beta-catenin destruction-complex component Apc in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut increased canonical Wnt feedback genes, including Axin2, Nkd1, and Notum, while altering neuronal transcripts such as Gls, Tagln3, Spock3, Bace2, Rgs16, and Olfm1. This is a clear positive control for Wnt derepression in a mature thalamic neuron class. The biological interpretation is that APC actively restrains beta-catenin target genes even weeks after neurogenesis.
significance: Wnt signaling is usually framed around development, synapse formation, and plasticity. An acute postmitotic Apc signature in thalamus provides specific effectors for testing whether adult-like thalamic excitatory neurons keep Wnt feedback under active destruction-complex control.
prior_expectation: APC is the canonical scaffold that promotes beta-catenin degradation, so Apc loss should increase Axin2 and Nkd1. The novelty is the in vivo cell class and the coupling of Wnt feedback to thalamic metabolic and synaptic transcripts.
support_and_caveats: Apc in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut used 187 perturbed nuclei, changed 263 genes, and had 71 stringent genes. The expected Wnt targets were prominent: Axin2 +1.25, FDR 2.43e-16; Nkd1 +2.45, FDR 2.14e-13; and Notum +1.56 among FDR-significant genes. Other high-scoring rows were Atrnl1 +0.64, FDR 9.18e-17; Serpine2 +1.56, FDR 1.94e-16; Gls -0.50, FDR 1.17e-12; and Bace2 +2.29, FDR 1.30e-10. The pathway direction is internally consistent, but the dataset cannot infer whether altered beta-catenin-dependent transcription is cell-autonomous at these loci without chromatin validation.
research_community: Wnt/beta-catenin neurobiology labs and thalamic development groups would be the main audience. Experiments should test beta-catenin stabilization by immunostaining, TCF/LEF reporter activation in Prkcd/Grin2c neurons, and whether Apc loss changes thalamic afferent or efferent synapse physiology.

finding_title: Ogt loss represses RNA-processing and cholesterol-turnover transcripts while relieving Xpo1
core_idea: Perturbing O-GlcNAc transferase changed 1,472 genes across 19 classes. The direct observation is repeated loss of Ogt, Rsrp1, Snhg11, Kifc2, Odf2, Rbm14, Leng8, Oga, Cyp46a1, and Srrm2, together with induction of Xpo1 and Nap1l5. The interpretation is that O-GlcNAc cycling is required in postnatal neurons to maintain RNA-processing factors and cholesterol-turnover transcripts, not only cytosolic signaling proteins.
significance: Neuronal O-GlcNAcylation has been linked to memory and brain aging; the atlas defines an early molecular state after acute OGT loss in many neuronal classes. The unexpected overlap with nuclear transport and RNA splicing makes Ogt a bridge between metabolic sensing and RNA homeostasis.
prior_expectation: Temporally controlled neuron-specific OGT knockout in mice recapitulates cellular and cognitive features of brain aging, whereas viral OGT overexpression can improve memory in aged hippocampus (Wheatley et al., 2019, PMID: 31588002). The prior did not specify a recurrent Rsrp1/Xpo1/Cyp46a1 signature.
support_and_caveats: The largest Ogt signatures were in 155 MB Glut (536 genes), 191 MB P MY GABA (316), and 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA (285). In 155 MB Glut, Ogt itself was -1.68, q = 3.09e-23; Xpo1 +1.52, q = 3.46e-20; Rsrp1 -0.901, q = 4.12e-17; Leng8 -0.898, q = 3.01e-15; Srrm2 -0.952, q = 1.89e-12; Odf2 -1.28, q = 1.89e-12; and Kifc2 -1.02, q = 7.71e-10. In 191 MB P MY GABA, Ogt was -2.42, q = 2.88e-21; Rsrp1 -1.05, q = 4.87e-11; Xpo1 +1.31, q = 5.73e-09; and Cyp46a1 -1.45, q = 6.08e-07. O-GlcNAcylation itself was not measured, so this is an inferred consequence of reduced OGT.
research_community: O-GlcNAc, neurodegeneration, brain aging, RNA-processing, and metabolic neuroscience groups are likely to follow this. The clean next step is to pair Ogt CRISPR with O-GlcNAc proteomics, OGA inhibition or substrate rescue, and isoform sequencing to test whether RSRP1/SRRM2 loss is transcriptional, splicing-mediated, or selection for damaged neurons.

finding_title: Elp1 perturbation activates an amino-acid starvation and integrated-stress-like program in thalamic glutamatergic neurons
core_idea: Elp1 loss in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut up-regulated aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase, amino-acid transport, one-carbon, and ER-stress genes. The top induced genes included Cars, Asns, Shmt2, Slc1a4, Slc3a2, Slc38a2, Herpud1, Ddit3, and Mars1, while Adgrb1 was reduced. The result suggests that Elongator dysfunction in a mature thalamic class engages amino-acid deprivation and ER stress before overt cell loss.
significance: ELP1 is central to familial dysautonomia and sensory/autonomic neuron development, but this postnatal central thalamic stress module is not the classical peripheral-neuron phenotype. It points to a convergent stress state that can be compared with tRNA-modification defects and integrated stress response inhibitors.
prior_expectation: ELP1/IKBKAP is required cell-autonomously for sympathetic and sensory neuron innervation (Jackson et al., 2014, PMID:24917501), and mouse models show a requirement for Elp1 in visceral sensory peripheral and central circuitry (Tolman et al., 2022, PMID:35481599). A central postmitotic thalamic amino-acid response was plausible but not established.
support_and_caveats: Elp1 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut used 153 perturbed nuclei, changed 570 genes, and had 152 genes at FDR < 1e-4. High-scoring rows were Cars +1.12, FDR 1.53e-28; Chac1 +3.43, FDR 2.28e-28; Asns +1.46, FDR 1.50e-27; Shmt2 +2.26, FDR 3.49e-22; Slc1a4 +2.23, FDR 2.87e-21; Herpud1 +0.98, FDR 4.76e-21; Adgrb1 -0.68, FDR 1.32e-20; Ddit3 +1.57, FDR 3.13e-20; and Slc38a2 +1.03, FDR 1.82e-16. The pattern is consistent with integrated stress, but ATF4 protein and eIF2alpha phosphorylation were not measured.
research_community: Familial dysautonomia investigators, Elongator/tRNA-modification groups, and integrated-stress-response labs would be interested. Follow-up should test ATF4/CHOP activation after Elp1 loss, profile tRNA wobble-uridine modifications in sorted neurons, and ask whether ISRIB-like modulation rescues the Asns/Chac1 module without worsening survival.

finding_title: Kansl1 loss perturbs midbrain lysosomal and Golgi trafficking transcripts
core_idea: The NSL histone-acetyltransferase complex subunit Kansl1 produced a midbrain glutamatergic signature with decreased Nsmce2, Ccdc39, Smpd4, Ergic3, Stx8, Commd4, Exoc1, Pik3c3, Ctsa, and Man2b2, plus increases in genes such as Dgkz, Tspoap1, Son, and Ank2. The program points toward lysosome, ER-Golgi, and autophagy-associated traffic rather than a broad global transcriptional collapse. It implies that KANSL1 haploinsufficiency can acutely disturb membrane-turnover genes in postnatal midbrain neurons.
significance: KANSL1 causes Koolen-de Vries syndrome and has been linked to autophagosome-lysosome fusion in mouse models. The atlas independently finds a lysosomal/traffic signature in a defined mature neuronal population, strengthening the case that autophagy-related rescue should be assessed in neurons and not only bulk tissue.
prior_expectation: KANSL1 haploinsufficiency causes Koolen-de Vries syndrome; mouse Kansl1 haploinsufficiency impairs autophagosome-lysosome fusion and mitophagic clearance through transcriptional regulation of autophagy genes such as Stx17 (Li et al., 2022, PMID:35177641). Thus a trafficking signature was expected, but its exact midbrain form was new.
support_and_caveats: Kansl1 in 155 MB Glut used 113 perturbed nuclei, changed 350 genes, and had 39 stringent genes. Examples included Nsmce2 -1.33, FDR 2.62e-10; Ccdc39 -1.81, FDR 1.04e-09; Ttc4 -0.80, FDR 8.55e-09; Dgkz +0.82, FDR 1.02e-08; Smpd4 -1.13, FDR 1.10e-08; Son +0.54, FDR 2.33e-07; Ergic3 -0.89, FDR 2.79e-07; Stx8 -1.19, FDR 3.41e-07; and Commd4 -1.15, FDR 6.34e-07. The signature is weaker than Setd1a or Sin3a and lacks direct lysosomal flux measurements.
research_community: Koolen-de Vries syndrome, autophagy, and chromatin-regulatory-complex groups are the likely audience. Follow-ups should test whether retinoic-acid or lysosomal-fusion interventions rescue the midbrain signature, and should map KANSL1/KAT8 histone-acetylation changes near vesicle-fusion genes.

finding_title: Atp6v0c loss coordinately reduces V-ATPase and calcium-channel transcripts
core_idea: The V-ATPase V0 subunit perturbation Atp6v0c had an unusually recurrent target response, with Atp6v0c itself lower in 22 classes and Atp6v0a1 lower in 12. The strongest downstream effects were in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, where calcium and GABA-related transcripts including Atp2a2, Prkcg, Prkcd, and Gabrd were also repressed. The interpretation is that partial lysosomal proton-pump disruption feeds back on V-ATPase subunit expression and neuronal excitability genes.
significance: V-ATPase genes are central to lysosome biology but have been hard to place in specific neuronal transcriptomes. This perturbation nominates a cell-class-specific acidification-to-excitability path that can be validated with lysosomal pH and channel physiology.
prior_expectation: The TFEB/V-ATPase axis is known to coordinate lysosomal function and development, and ATP6V0C impairment can alter the endolysosomal compartment in human epithelial cells (Tognon et al., 2016, PMID: 26727288). A coherent thalamic Prkcd/Gabrd calcium-channel module was less expected.
support_and_caveats: Atp6v0c produced 755 changed genes across 22 classes, with 490 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 151 in 052 Pvalb Gaba. In thalamic neurons, Atp6v0c was -1.43, q = 1.04e-34; Atp2a2 -0.577, q = 3.09e-20; Atp6v0a1 -0.577, q = 2.39e-19; Pcp4 -0.957, q = 1.36e-17; Prkcg -0.856, q = 1.56e-16; Cadm4 -0.758, q = 1.14e-13; Prkcd -0.699, q = 1.22e-12; and Gabrd -0.697, q = 1.71e-12. Atp6v0a1 was also down in Pvalb neurons (-0.450, q = 1.29e-07). Because V-ATPase loss can alter viability, late degenerative repression is a plausible alternative.
research_community: Lysosome, V-ATPase, epileptic encephalopathy, and thalamic-circuit groups would pursue this. Follow-up should quantify lysosomal pH and membrane potential after Atp6v0c loss, rescue with pump-dead versus pump-active ATP6V0C, and measure whether GABA-A delta subunit and PRKCG loss change thalamic firing.

finding_title: Rab7 loss elicits a lysosomal hydrolase and sterol-response state
core_idea: Rab7 perturbation was dominated by a thalamic signature that induced Atp6v1b2, Dpp7, Scpep1, Insig1, Atp6v0b, Slc20a1, and Dync1h1, with a smaller matching midbrain program containing Lamp2, Grn, Mcoln1, and Rab7 itself. The observation supports a model in which late-endosome transport stress triggers lysosomal and cholesterol-sensing compensation in neurons. The interpretation is narrower than for TSC: Rab7 likely affects endosome-lysosome maturation upstream of the sterol module.
significance: The Rab7 response connects a core trafficking GTPase to the same lysosome/sterol genes seen after TSC perturbation, providing an epistasis opportunity. If RAB7 and mTORC1 converge on Atp6v0b, Dpp7, and Insig1, this could identify druggable lysosomal feedback that is common to several disease genes.
prior_expectation: RAB7 is required for endosome-lysosome trafficking and lysosome reformation; in GBA1-deficient Parkinson disease models, Rab7 accumulates with lysosomal recycling failure and altered cholesterol homeostasis (Magalhaes et al., 2016, PMID: 27378698). The exact acute neuron signature was not directly known.
support_and_caveats: Rab7 had 436 changed genes across 7 cell classes, with 361 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut. In that thalamic class, Atp6v1b2 was +0.443, q = 1.06e-16; Dpp7 +0.904, q = 6.11e-16; Scpep1 +1.57, q = 5.18e-15; Dusp1 +1.25, q = 1.20e-14; Insig1 +0.948, q = 1.87e-13; and Atp6v0b +0.322, q = 4.26e-13. In 155 MB Glut, Atp6v0b was +0.372, q = 4.15e-11; Dpp7 +0.888, q = 7.29e-08; Lamp2 +0.600, q = 1.44e-07; Grn +0.935, q = 2.18e-07; and Mcoln1 +0.455, q = 1.67e-06. Support is lower than for TSC because one thalamic class accounts for most DE genes.
research_community: Endolysosomal trafficking, Parkinson disease, autophagy, and neuronal lipid investigators would be the main audience. The most informative follow-up would test Rab7 x Tsc1 genetic interactions, live-cell lysosome motility, mTORC1 recruitment to lysosomes, and sterol reporters in the same neuronal subtypes.

finding_title: Rnpc3 loss creates a core spliceosome response centered on Mapk8, Ap2a1, Wdfy1, Pcyt2, and Pten
core_idea: Rnpc3, a U11/U12 spliceosome component, produced its strongest response in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, with additional midbrain and GABAergic responses. The thalamic signature decreased Rnpc3 and increased Mapk8, Ap2a1, Pcyt2, Wdfy1, Srp72, Trit1, Vash2, and Pten. The interpretation is that minor-spliceosome stress in mature thalamic neurons engages JNK, clathrin-adaptor, phospholipid, and PTEN-associated pathways.
significance: This finding broadens the RNA-processing theme beyond SR factors and identifies a distinct downstream pattern from Srsf1. Because minor introns are enriched in regulatory genes, this is a useful hypothesis for why partial defects in a rare spliceosome component might have amplified neuronal consequences.
prior_expectation: Alternative splicing is central to neuronal maturation, and SRSF1/PTBP2-like cascades were already known in developing cortex (Weber et al., 2023, PMID:37697438). A U11/U12-specific factor such as RNPC3 would be expected to cause RNA-processing stress, but the Mapk8/Ap2a1/Pten axis is more specific.
support_and_caveats: Rnpc3 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut used 149 perturbed nuclei, changed 820 genes, and retained 236 stringent genes. Top rows were Rnpc3 -1.69, FDR 3.22e-39; Amy1 -2.10, FDR 1.84e-37; Mapk8 +1.76, FDR 6.03e-37; Ap2a1 +1.37, FDR 3.93e-36; Pcyt2 +1.82, FDR 1.30e-34; Wdfy1 +1.89, FDR 2.71e-33; and Pten +0.92, FDR 2.47e-21. Rnpc3 also changed 221 genes in 155 MB Glut, 77 in 052 Pvalb Gaba, 73 in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, and 55 in 191 MB P MY GABA. Long-read sequencing is required to show that minor intron retention drives these abundance changes.
research_community: Minor-spliceosome, RNA surveillance, and neuronal PTEN/mTOR researchers would be motivated. Experiments should quantify U12 intron retention, test JNK inhibition, and ask whether Pten induction is a compensatory brake on stress-induced growth pathways.

finding_title: U2af2 perturbation depresses spliceosomal and calcium-handling genes in thalamic and midbrain neurons
core_idea: The major-spliceosome factor U2af2 produced parallel responses in thalamic, midbrain glutamatergic, and midbrain GABA classes. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, the strongest decreased genes included Rsrp1, Srrm2, Atp2a2, Agrn, Luc7l2, Srsf11, and Atp11b, while Map7d1, Iffo1, and Copb1 increased. This supports a second, mechanistically distinct spliceosome-to-synaptic-homeostasis relationship.
significance: U2af2 sits at the 3-prime splice-site recognition step, so its in vivo downstream genes can separate general spliceosome failure from SRSF1-specific or minor-spliceosome programs. The thalamic and midbrain signatures nominate Atp2a2 and Agrn as vulnerable mature-neuron transcripts after splice-site recognition stress.
prior_expectation: Splicing factors have broad RNA targets and are essential for neuronal isoform diversity; published transcriptome compendia have shown that perturbing splicing factors creates identifiable expression signatures (Yu et al., 2020, PMID:32546682). A large signature after U2af2 loss is not surprising, but the recurrent calcium and extracellular-matrix components add specificity.
support_and_caveats: U2af2 changed 650 genes in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut with 222 perturbed nuclei, 744 in 155 MB Glut with 187 nuclei, and 398 in 191 MB P MY GABA with 85 nuclei. Thalamic high-scoring rows included Rsrp1 -0.98, FDR 9.01e-29; Srrm2 -0.44, FDR 8.73e-17; Map7d1 +0.65, FDR 8.73e-17; Atp2a2 -0.47, FDR 9.74e-16; Agrn -0.56, FDR 1.13e-14; Luc7l2 -0.45, FDR 9.39e-13; and Atp11b -0.72, FDR 1.01e-12. As with Srsf1, the snRNA-seq assay cannot distinguish isoform switching from total mRNA changes.
research_community: Spliceosome structural groups, RNA-therapeutic developers, and neuronal calcium-homeostasis labs would be interested. Follow-up should use nanopore cDNA or targeted RT-PCR panels to test whether Atp2a2 or Agrn isoforms are direct U2AF2-sensitive transcripts.

finding_title: Prdm10 perturbation reveals a conserved Madd, Cadm3, Ptov1, Stmn2, Myt1, and Uchl1 repression signature
core_idea: Prdm10 disruption generated a small but very coherent signature across 10 classes. The observed result was recurrent down-regulation of Madd, Cadm3, Ptov1, Stmn2, Myt1, Uchl1, Them6, and Ackr1, with Madd significant in all 10 classes and Cadm3 and Ptov1 in 9. The biological interpretation is that PRDM10 sustains a mature axonal and cell-adhesion gene module in multiple neuronal types.
significance: PRDM-family chromatin factors are plausible disease genes but PRDM10 has much less mature-neuron biology than many regulators in the screen. The atlas elevates it by identifying a precise downstream module that recurs despite only 182 significant rows.
prior_expectation: PRDM proteins often act as transcriptional and chromatin regulators, so a targeted gene-expression effect was plausible. PubMed did not reveal a direct neuronal Prdm10 -> Madd/Cadm3/Ptov1 precedent, making the relationship a relatively novel atlas-derived finding.
support_and_caveats: Prdm10 had significant signatures in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, 155 MB Glut, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 145 MH-LH TH Glut, 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, and 052 Pvalb Gaba. Madd was down in 10 classes, median log2FC -1.28, min q=8.7e-42; Cadm3 was down in 9, median -0.99, min q=2.3e-36; Ptov1 was down in 9, median -1.27, min q=3.6e-30; and Stmn2 was down in 7, min q=7.4e-18. The signature is compact, so it needs more sensitivity to reveal whether PRDM10 has broader direct targets.
research_community: Chromatin and axonal maintenance groups would be best suited to pursue this. A strong experiment would validate PRDM10 binding at Madd, Cadm3, and Stmn2, then assay axon maintenance and cell-adhesion phenotypes after direct disruption of each candidate effector.

finding_title: Rora loss acutely represses Prkcg, Rasa4, Tnnt1, and Pcp4 in Grin2c thalamic neurons
core_idea: The orphan nuclear receptor perturbation Rora yielded 261 changed genes, all in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut. The observation is downregulation of Prkcg, Adgrb1, Rasa4, Tnnt1, Plekhd1, Elmod1, Atp6ap2, Pcp4, and Kcnc2. The interpretation is that RORA, although classically tied to Purkinje cells, has an acute maintenance role in a non-cerebellar thalamic excitability program.
significance: This is a lower-breadth but provocative extension of RORA biology outside cerebellar Purkinje neurons. If validated, it argues that RORA-targeting ataxia therapeutics may need to account for thalamic neurons and their calcium/kinase transcripts.
prior_expectation: RORalpha is required for Purkinje-cell development and survival, and reduced RORalpha worsens SCA1 pathogenesis (Serra et al., 2006, PMID: 17110330; Doulazmi et al., 2006, PMID: 16807193). Purkinje vulnerability was expected; an acute Grin2c thalamic signature was not.
support_and_caveats: The only active class was 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, where Prkcg was -0.764, q = 9.68e-18; Adgrb1 -0.702, q = 1.35e-17; Rasa4 -1.54, q = 3.98e-16; Tnnt1 -1.70, q = 2.53e-14; Plekhd1 -1.51, q = 1.44e-13; Elmod1 -1.14, q = 6.61e-13; Atp6ap2 -0.643, q = 7.11e-13; Pcp4 -0.584, q = 3.72e-11; and Kcnc2 -0.355, q = 3.72e-10. The support score is only 3 because the effect is confined to one atlas class and Rora itself did not pass the significance threshold in this filtered table.
research_community: RORalpha/SCA, thalamic excitability, nuclear-receptor pharmacology, and calcium-signaling groups are the likely audience. The most direct validation would use RNAscope and RORA ChIP/CUT&Tag in Prkcd/Grin2c thalamus, then test whether RORalpha agonists rescue the Prkcg/Pcp4/Kcnc2 state.

finding_title: Zfp423 loss disrupts Grid2ip/Cd47 and derepresses Ntsr1 in Prkcd/Grin2c thalamic neurons
core_idea: Zfp423 perturbation in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut reduced Grid2ip, Cd47, Syt13, Cnnm1, Pxdn, Mpi, Adgrb2, and Grin2c, and strongly increased Ntsr1, Kcnab3, Nptxr, and Scn1b. The observation suggests that ZFP423, known for developmental cerebellar functions, continues to regulate a postnatal thalamic identity module and suppresses corticothalamic-like Ntsr1 expression in this thalamic class.
significance: ZFP423 is classically tied to cerebellar development and ciliopathy/Joubert biology. A mature Prkcd/Grin2c thalamic response is therefore a high-novelty lead that could reveal an unappreciated role for this zinc-finger factor outside cerebellar progenitors and Purkinje cells.
prior_expectation: Zfp423 is required for normal cerebellar development in mice (Warming et al., 2006, PMID:16943432), and ZFP423/ZNF423 regulates cell-cycle progression and DNA-damage responses in Purkinje neuron progenitors (Casoni et al., 2017, PMID:28893945). Those studies did not predict a strong postnatal thalamic Grid2ip/Ntsr1 relationship.
support_and_caveats: Zfp423 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut used 160 perturbed nuclei, changed 139 genes, and retained 40 stringent genes. Top rows were Grid2ip -1.27, FDR 3.07e-45; Cd47 -0.99, FDR 1.27e-35; Ntsr1 +5.14, FDR 5.89e-21; Kcnab3 +1.39, FDR 4.34e-17; Syt13 -0.89, FDR 2.62e-15; Nptxr +1.00, FDR 4.98e-15; Pxdn -1.47, FDR 8.79e-14; Scn1b +0.37, FDR 1.09e-10; and Grin2c -0.57, FDR 1.65e-10. The signature is specific but smaller than top-ranked chromatin signatures, and the increase in a sparse marker such as Ntsr1 needs single-molecule validation.
research_community: Cerebellar-development, ciliopathy, and thalamic-identity groups would be the best audience. Experiments should map ZFP423 binding near Grid2ip and Ntsr1, repeat the perturbation in adult thalamus, and ask whether ZFP423 loss shifts electrophysiological identity toward a corticothalamic-like state.

finding_title: TDP-43 loss induces Ppp6c, Gabpa, and trafficking transcripts while repressing Snrnp70
core_idea: Tardbp perturbation produced 533 changed genes across 16 classes. The direct observation is downregulation of Tardbp and Snrnp70, with upregulation of Ppp6c, Fam219a, Brms1l, Uggt2, Usp15, Gabpa, Abcc5, Fam135a, Sec24b, Kifbp, and Unc13a. The interpretation is that partial nuclear TDP-43 loss causes a compensatory phosphatase/trafficking RNA program in multiple postnatal neuronal classes.
significance: TDP-43 nuclear depletion is central to ALS/FTD. Although this atlas does not assay cryptic exons, it offers an in vivo mouse brain perturbation signature that can be aligned against human TDP-43 loss-of-function datasets.
prior_expectation: Nuclear TDP-43 represses cryptic exon inclusion, with direct disease links through UNC13A and STMN2 misprocessing (Ma et al., 2022, PMID: 35197626; Baughn et al., 2023, PMID: 36927019). A coding-gene DE signature was plausible but less established than splicing changes.
support_and_caveats: Tardbp changed 187 genes in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 96 in 191 MB P MY GABA, and 89 in 155 MB Glut, with smaller signatures across 13 more classes. In thalamic neurons, Ppp6c was +1.98, q = 2.45e-41; Tardbp -1.41, q = 1.60e-39; Gabpa +2.25, q = 1.74e-38; Usp15 +0.978, q = 8.87e-37; Fam135a +2.13, q = 4.16e-35; Brms1l +1.24, q = 2.02e-32; Uggt2 +1.36, q = 7.38e-32; and Abcc5 +0.548, q = 3.03e-27. Ppp6c and Fam135a repeated in 191 MB P MY GABA. The support is incomplete because the canonical cryptic-splicing consequences of TDP-43 loss are invisible in this DE table.
research_community: ALS/FTD, TDP-43, neuronal RNA-splicing, and antisense-therapy groups are obvious. Follow-up should perform long-read and targeted cryptic-exon assays on the same Tardbp-perturbed nuclei, then compare whether the DE signature tracks with UNC13A/STMN2-like splicing rescue or with separate cellular stress.
